leads.why: The equal balance grouping finds only faces with a one to one unit. The group test for other ratios was limited to 170 tokens by the 100,000 byte cap on return data. A probe contract that returns one changed flag per token would lift the limit.

leads.question: When the C-Chain rule set for Igloo is published: does it include ACP-209, a new precompile at 0x0200000000000000000000000000000000000006, new opcodes or a change to the storage partition rule of finding F-040?
leads.why: Igloo is the only named upgrade and has no public C-Chain scope. Set code accounts and a precompile that takes value for a named account are the two parts of ACP-209 that meet the PoolManager call shapes.

leads.question: After Lagoon activates on OP Sepolia and Unichain Sepolia (target 10 December 2026), and again on OP Mainnet and Unichain (target 11 January 2027): which implementations sit behind 0x4200..0022 to 0x4200..0028 and 0x4200..0030, and what does each return to the sixteen call shapes with the PoolManager as msg.sender? Confirm from the deployed bytecode that ETHLiquidity, SuperchainETHBridge and SuperchainTokenBridge have no receive or fallback and none of the selectors the PoolManager can send.
leads.why: The clearance of this cycle was read from source on the develop branch and from op-contracts v4.0.0, because the contracts are not deployed. A fallback or a payable receive in the installed version would make one of them a native payout recipient that books value to the PoolManager, the shape of F-048.

attempts.answer: Lagoon is not active on any of the four networks. The implementation slots of the interop predeploys are zero on OP Mainnet, Unichain, OP Sepolia and Unichain Sepolia on 2026-11-23, and the registry lists Lagoon as not scheduled. The question can be answered after the Sepolia activation targeted for 10 December 2026.

leads.question: Build the list of all pool currencies of the Base PoolManager from the full Initialize history with an archive log source that allows wide ranges (an indexer export or a paid endpoint), then rerun the reconcile script and the trigger probe of this cycle over it.
leads.why: Public sources cannot do it: the Tenderly gateway caps eth_getLogs at 1,000 blocks without an access code, mainnet.base.org answered 'request limit reached', and base.blockscout.com answers HTTP 403. Base has about 61 million blocks and the largest pool count of the unit. The tested list holds the 9,108 tokens that moved in one day.

attempts.answer: The Base list is built: 15,540,638 pools, 15,315,529 currencies, no failed window, twelve windows confirmed on a second endpoint. The Tenderly gateway answers 1,000 block windows fast enough to read the whole history in about 15 minutes. The sweeps ran on 59,170 currencies chosen by code hash and code size. A new lead asks for the per token tests of the mass templates.

leads.question: Build the list of all pool currencies of the World Chain PoolManager from the full Initialize history. The public endpoint caps eth_getLogs at 100 blocks.
leads.why: The tested list is the explorer holdings page with 851 tokens. A pooled token that the explorer does not index was never tested.

leads.question: For the Base hooks 0xbdf938149ac6a781f94faa0ed45e6a0e984c6544, 0x0469a4bd3724dc86c9542f4694c976da13c450c0, 0xb429d62f8f3bffb98cdb9569533ea23bf0ba28cc and 0x5e320ea6278107968c119942e57d876c5f922acc: which contract is allowed to initialize pools, can an ordinary account reach that path with a paired currency of its own choice, and what do beforeSwap and afterSwap of 0xb429 and 0x5e32 (both return deltas) do with the hook's ERC-6909 claims?
leads.why: A direct initialize from an ordinary account reverts in all four, which rules out the simplest case only. The sources were not read because the Base explorer API was not reachable. 0xb429 already holds small WETH and USDC claims at the PoolManager.

leads.question: For the pooled tokens whose balanceOf reads a second contract (an exchange, a vault, a rate provider or an oracle): which of those second contracts has a public function that raises the reported balance of every holder? List them by tracing balanceOf(PoolManager) for the tokens with the largest balances on the endpoints that serve debug_traceCall.
leads.why: The trigger probe of this cycle called 70 functions on the token contract itself and found nothing on 19,664 tokens. A rebase that is triggered on another contract, as with USD+ and its exchange, is outside that probe. A public trigger would let a caller run sync, the trigger and settle and take the whole increase (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364).

leads.question: Once interop is live, do any routers, intent settlers or bridges on OP Mainnet or Unichain send tokens or ETH to the PoolManager in one cross-chain message and call settle in a later step or a later message?
leads.why: Relays are permissionless. An account that executes such a relay inside its own unlock, after its own sync, is credited the payment (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364). Core is safe, so this concerns periphery that will be written for the fork.

leads.question: When Everest gets an activation time, read the Base Transaction executor again on the release that carries it: does sender and payer authorization still require a secp256k1 signature of that account, and does gas-limit billing change who is debited?
leads.why: The file crates/common/evm/src/eip8130.rs exists at v1.5.6 and returns HTTP 404 on the main branch, so the code has moved or changed since the reading of this cycle. A payer that can be named without its own signature would let the protocol debit an arbitrary account's ETH.

leads.question: Which op-reth commit does the OP Mainnet sequencer run? The official endpoint and publicnode both report op-reth/v0.0.0-dev-unknown.
leads.why: Two released builds that follow the chain have now been read (commit 72fcf947 in cycle 2 and tag op-reth/v2.4.2 in this cycle). The block producer of the chain with the most value in this unit is still unidentified.

leads.question: On every new Base node release and at every fork that adds a B20 logic version or a new stateful precompile: does a DELEGATECALL or CALLCODE to a B20 token, to the B20 factory and to the Policy Registry, made by a contract that the PoolManager has called, still revert, and does the token still take the direct caller as the source of transfer?
leads.why: The PoolManager calls contracts chosen by any account (src/PoolManager.sol:110, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134, src/types/Currency.sol:48). In such a frame msg.sender is the PoolManager. At base v1.5.6 one check in the macro base_precompile (input.is_direct_call()) stops that frame from forwarding the PoolManager's identity into the token, and on 23 November 2026 the PoolManager held 5,322,585 OUSD at 0xB2000000000000000000002fEb517dFeC7415344. A release that drops or bypasses the check would let any account move that balance. The test of this cycle is a single read-only eth_call with two state overrides and can be repeated in seconds.

leads.question: Does revm at the exact version 41.0.0 that op-reth v2.4.2 pins clear transient storage in commit_tx and discard_tx, as the main branch does?
leads.why: The verifier read crates/context/src/journal/inner.rs on the main branch of revm, where both functions call transient_storage.clear(). The file at the pinned version was not read because the matching tag was not identified.

leads.question: Which pooled tokens have a lock, grant or clawback function whose selector the signature database could not name, or whose arguments the fixed patterns did not fit? Take the 52,820 unnamed selectors from the work directory, keep those in tokens with a balance above 1,000 USD, and read the verified sources.
leads.why: The two findings of this unit came from functions with well known names. A token with a private naming scheme and the same balanceOf design would give the same freeze or the same clawback and was not tested.

leads.question: Since which block do yUSD, yETH and xSolvBTC reject the PoolManager, which pools hold them, and does the YieldFi list name the PoolManager address or all contracts?
leads.why: About 976,000 USD at price service figures sits behind these three blocks. The answer shows whether issuers block the singleton on purpose, which would repeat on the new address.

attempts.answer: yUSD and yETH reject the PoolManager since block 24,283,369 (2026-01-21 13:09:23 UTC) and xSolvBTC since block 25,518,435 (2026-07-12 18:48:59 UTC). Both lists name the PoolManager address itself: the YieldFi transaction 0xf46bcb77... passes an array of two addresses, one account without code and the PoolManager, to blackListUsers, and the Solv transaction 0xc00cb1f2... is a Safe execution that adds the PoolManager to the token's list. Pools: yUSD 60 (5 with active liquidity), yETH 16 (3), xSolvBTC 16 (5). A new PoolManager address starts unlisted. Details are in the F-080 addition of this file, which also records that ankrETH is paused for all senders since block 26,376,473.

leads.question: Rerun the own transfer test and finish the full balance transfer test on Robinhood Chain, Elysium and Arc, and fetch code for every distinct hash on Robinhood Chain in place of the size sample.
leads.why: These three networks hold 1.13 million of the 1.24 million pooled currencies and were covered through families and samples.

leads.question: What is TITHE worth, which pools hold it, and do the three other tokens with its selector set pay rewards to the PoolManager as well?
leads.why: 10,002.56 TITHE can be booked by anyone today. The value decides whether this is a live extraction.

leads.question: Which tokens raise the PoolManager balance only at certain times or after a deposit of a second asset: vault shares with a deposit for function and a holding period for the receiver, reward tokens with nothing due at the time of the test, rebases whose epoch was not due?
leads.why: The trial sweep sees a trigger only when it has an effect in the block of the test and only when the caller needs nothing but the token itself.

leads.question: Which pooled tokens create a lock on the recipient when a distributor, auction, airdrop or vesting contract transfers to an address that an ordinary caller names? Start from FOLD 0xe172e9b6cfbeeb5593bdce3f077356fdb33af904 on Ethereum, where a transfer from CLAIM_SOURCE 0x687cc38d8279df3352b64cf3ec1fe8e033933595 locks the amount at the recipient and the auction pays the bid owner that the bidder chose. List the tokens whose transfer hook treats one sender specially, read that sender, and check whether claim, claimTo, claimFor, release or exit functions on it pay an address chosen by the caller. For FOLD, check the ten bids that are not exited and any later claim source the owner could set.
leads.why: The trial sweep of this cycle called functions of the token only. A lock that arrives through a third contract gives the same exchange of locked for liquid units as the QANX finding and adds a gain for the caller, because the locked amount comes from the caller's own allocation. Tokens sold through the same auction contract with claim locks would be exposed on the new deployment as soon as a pool holds liquid units while claims are open. For FOLD the path is closed today: no bid names the PoolManager and the auction is over.

attempts.answer: FOLD is closed and was read again at block 26,480,257: the claim source can be set once, the auction is over, none of its 310 bids names the PoolManager, and the PoolManager holds no lock. New fact: the claim source is a ContinuousClearingAuction, whose submitBid lets the bidder name any owner and whose claimTokens anyone can call after the claim block. The general question, which other pooled tokens lock what one special sender transfers, was not answered: I did not list transfer hooks that treat one sender specially on any network, and I did not enumerate other auctions of this contract type. That part is passed on as a lead.

leads.question: Do holders of locked QANX with allowedHops of at least 1 exist on 0xaaa7a10a8ee237ea61e8ac46c50a8db8bcc1baaa and 0xaaa9214f675316182eaa21c85f0ca99160cc3aaa? Read the LockApplied logs and lockOf for the recipients, and state how much locked QANX could be sent to the PoolManager under transferLocked.
leads.why: Both contracts let a sender pay a locked transfer from its own locked balance. Such a holder can book locked units between sync and settle (src/PoolManager.sol:358-364) and take liquid ones (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297), which turns the freeze of the QANX finding into a gain at the expense of the pools.

leads.question: On World Chain the trial sweep recorded that an ordinary account which had just received a third of the PoolManager balance gained 1,874,084 units from withdrawDividend() on 0x5b51b28cb3b7d3dfa2463f3df7ce3929c1464f1b and 2,429.9 units from claimDividend() on 0x98b440dc0491e076ab029bf9fc502a5a721ccce1, with the PoolManager balance unchanged (raw/assign_480.json.gz, class A-gain). Does the payout scale with the balance held at the time of the call, where does it come from, and does it have a price?
leads.why: If a holder of the moment can claim, any account can borrow the whole pooled balance with take, claim the dividend and settle in one unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297), which is assumption A5. The payout would come from the token's reward pot and not from pools, so this is a low item. I did not rerun these two trials. The same class in the sweep contains false hits where the test account 0x00000000000000000000000000000000000a11ce already held a balance, for example 29 USDC on Base.

leads.question: Capture the transaction that the hosted Uniswap web application proposes for removing a position in a pool whose token refuses transfers from the PoolManager (G$ on Celo position 178, ViciCoin on Polygon position 60652) and decode its action list. Does it ever use CLEAR_OR_TAKE or MINT_POSITION_FROM_DELTAS, and what does the interface show when the simulation of TAKE_PAIR fails?
leads.why: The published SDK builds removals that end in TAKE_PAIR only. If the application does the same, a block on one token locks the other currency of each position for every user who cannot build a call by hand. The finding rests on the SDK reading for this one link.

leads.question: Decompile the EIP-7702 delegate 0xb0c75276657e80ff04c98a3809dfc39a409a8736 on Ethereum: which handlers run when transient slot 0 is empty, and can any of them make the account call PoolManager.burn with the account 0x82ccba35ad0c7a62230ef8ff337ac67f4cce0ea5 as from?
leads.why: 47 delegated accounts are operators of that account. One handler already makes them call PoolManager.take to any caller. A second handler that burns the owner's claims would let any account pair the two inside its own unlock and take about 740 USD of claims.

leads.question: Read the unlockCallback of the unverified contracts whose public entry reached unlock in the trace and whose burn target was not observed: on Ethereum the routers 0xbc22993a15e16acbf12873f234510d35948f7a59, 0x4531332adecf255c66b5bf6485db73f894ed93d2, 0xad445acd8e2446c652fb47b2d4c5ee9973b150c9 and the implementation 0xa62f9b597225779b430024398b70374e8468ce14 behind proxy 0x37bfb8ac7c960e558657871d41ca70e07e7dbfff, on Robinhood Chain the 47,585 byte hooks with collectPlatform(bytes32[]) and the implementation 0x6b68d5061329f64a087fc894355cb1eacf2a2321. Which account does each burn or transferFrom name, and who chooses it?
leads.why: The reach test used six argument fillings and cannot follow a callback that needs a well formed struct. These contracts hold operator rights from 2 to 7 owners each and are the part of the census that rests on a negative trace alone.

attempts.answer: Ethereum part answered by replaying mined transactions with a call tracer from the original sender and from an unrelated account. The three routers name their own caller in burn, mint and take, and the proxy 0x37bfb8ac names itself. No traced call debits an owner who approved the contract unless that owner sent the transaction. The Robinhood Chain contracts of the lead were not read and are passed on as a lead.

leads.question: Repeat the claim balance step for BNB Smart Chain with an indexed log source, and price the 2,100 unpriced owner and id pairs on Robinhood Chain.
leads.why: The BNB Smart Chain gateway gave differing answers for 1,274 of 17,870 windows, so an id with a balance may be missing. The Robinhood Chain value figure covers 70 of 2,170 pairs.

leads.question: Will the build of this repository be deployed with the existing periphery addresses as its routers, and does any later Universal Router or PositionManager release handle BURN_6909 with a payer that the caller names?
leads.why: The census describes the PoolManagers that run today. A new PoolManager starts with no approvals. The Universal Router already holds an operator right on Robinhood Chain and allowances on Base, and they are harmless only because its code has no call to burn or transferFrom.

leads.question: Which approved operator or spender contracts build the burn or transferFrom selector at run time (signature strings such as burn(address,uint256,uint256) hashed in code, or a selector taken from calldata), and for each of them is the debited account always the caller?
leads.why: The census excluded contracts by searching bytecode for the constants 0xf5298aca and 0xfe99049a. That test missed 0x2834c56d948f063564ff0a3c29483db50c73045a on Robinhood Chain, which holds 120 unlimited allowances and calls burn through a hashed string. My reading clears that contract, and the same test was the stated reason elsewhere. A string search over all approved bytecode and a trace of each hit would close the gap.

leads.question: What calldata does the hosted Uniswap interface or its liquidity API return for a removal when a simulation of TAKE_PAIR fails, and does any widely used front end offer MINT_POSITION_FROM_DELTAS or CLEAR_OR_TAKE?
leads.why: The freeze of the paired currency in this unit's finding is confirmed for calldata built with the published SDK. Whether real users are stuck depends on the interface, which neither the researcher nor I captured.

leads.question: Which transactions left Klik hook 0x1d06faa7ff674ccfd8a5736c0c0973cb0a8fa0cc on Ethereum with 7798353546842757 claims of SPCXon against 79607629840677756 of pending fees, and the Unichain hook 0x9463925bdeee2be5eade2a60857442b4a15ca0cc 10000000000000000 UNI short? Read the ERC-6909 Transfer logs of the PoolManager with the hook as sender and the burn amounts per pool.
leads.why: The difference shows that pending fees of one token were already burned in the currency of other tokens. If one account did it on purpose, the payout step of the finding has been used and the severity should be judged on that.

attempts.answer: Unichain: one transaction, 0x2b6aab1368b9266b585e655377e5a9431b822e4ff4657fec34166824e372a82e in block 60,794,133, sent by 0x053d984eab3240cdf7c53b8b7846159f8146e99b through 0xec9a66a21a9c201bafa9a218b716403a27480409. In it the hook mints 0.01 units of id 0x29f2f95c696e93939d8ce77819377d16bd0dcc04 and burns 0.01 units of the UNI id, which is the whole 0.01 UNI difference. It is one use of the payout step that F-084 describes and not a series. Ethereum: the public endpoint returned no receipt for 0xd903d0ada1874646896a5191a2ef25accec3c3db1333914542b6ad9a8c96bfed, so the Ethereum half rests on the cycle 5 verdict and on F-096.

leads.question: In the Klik factories (0x20839c453a0ed8bcab1095ea068669469098297c on Tempo, 0xb6da931df2ed2c80db47923d4eb46fd913ee01c3 and 0x95e0da371711502eed78bcc3f17856b4415120ca on Ethereum and the factory() of each other hook): may any account call launch, and does collectFees(token) pay creatorFees[token] in pairOf(token) whatever currency the hook credited through creditCreatorFee?
leads.why: If both hold, an ordinary account that launches a token can turn fees credited in a worthless currency into the factory's balance of the real quote currency, which makes the payout step of the finding a direct gain. The Tempo factory holds 2946234 units of pathUSD.

attempts.answer: Yes to both parts. launch has no caller check in the verified KlikLauncher and AnyLauncher sources, and an eth_call from an ordinary account returns a token on the Ethereum and Tempo factories. collectFees(token) pays creatorFees[token] in pairOf[token], and creditCreatorFee records no currency, so fees credited in a worthless currency are paid in the real pair from the factory balance. Collected fees go to creatorOf[token]. Two Ethereum transactions (0xe91af1e1 and 0x341ecc66) took about 0.984 SPCXon and six other pair tokens this way, and the factory now records 0.9887 SPCXon of creator fees against a balance of 0.0043 SPCXon. On Tempo a simulated credit and collect moves the whole 2.946234 pathUSD of the factory.

leads.question: Repeat the debug_traceCall test of the finding on the Klik hooks 0x5b0a864213d49f23ed2a6635cc42b3b4fe7720cc and 0x64746dca345c5652bc251597bd99562216a7a0cc on Base, 0x71b7a448b96a01de73b0caf1267d33558d2620cc on Ink and Arbitrum One and 0xb2c964edbac922f006a09bd293b6c42ee147e0cc on Avalanche once a token has pending fees, with all pools of each hook listed from the Initialize logs.
leads.why: Only the open initialize was confirmed on these four networks. On Base the census kept three sample pools per hook, so tokens with pending fees may exist and were missed.

leads.question: For the launch pad hooks that keep fee ledgers and reject a direct initialize (0x6b1216a40b65c83e9c9e18a562c446697b8cf8ec, 0xe0def4221b9840a610d4e7d55812a79a6431a8ec and 0x3ab88ddc3cf2a012af88b60828edb4553697e5dc on Elysium, CashCatHookV2, PonsV2MemeHook, 0x4eb1976978756bd56802d8162f2271844924e0cc and 0x2c668601193e4a081dd82604785e436aff6a2acc on Robinhood Chain, WonkHook and MinaraFeeHook on Arc, TaxLaunchHook on X Layer, LaunchHook on Ethereum): can an ordinary account launch through the factory with a quote currency of its choice, and is each fee ledger stored per pool id or per token and currency?
leads.why: The Klik finding is a ledger stored per token and paid in the currency of the calling pool. Hooks that hold claims for thousands of pools and let the launcher pick the quote currency can have the same fault behind a factory gate. These hooks hold claims or balances today, for example 178 native units and 20.5 native claims at the first Elysium hook.

leads.question: Complete the hook census where it is partial: Base blocks 37,000,001 to 49,000,000 were sampled one window in four, and X Layer was read only for the most recent 1.4 million blocks because the public endpoints limit eth_getLogs to 100 blocks. Find an indexer or archive endpoint and rerun the count and the probe for the five most used hooks.
leads.why: A widely used hook that created its pools in the unread ranges would be missing from the top five. The X Layer hook named in lead L-258 created no pool in the window that was read.

leads.question: Do routers or interfaces list pools from allPools or getPoolCount of the ERC-4626 wrapper hooks (0xc9987661b047cd73e3b0d66b2b7615a2ca811088 on Polygon, 0x89fcd09773c7c46ea20887c5246033f8a0a1d088 on Arbitrum One, 0x987105e95645d39ad967c8698478e17861271088 on Optimism, 0x8d92ff0a753dbc32e5c9c9f6493a1410d83e1088 on Monad), and what does afterInitialize check about the vault besides asset()?
leads.why: Any account can register a pool for a vault contract it wrote. A swap through such a pool hands the input to that contract. That harms only users who are routed there, so it matters if a router trusts the hook's own list.

leads.question: List every transaction on the nine networks in which a Klik hook burns claims of one currency for an amount it minted in another currency, starting from Ethereum 0xd903d0ada1874646896a5191a2ef25accec3c3db1333914542b6ad9a8c96bfed (sender 0x6356bab9f082de9abf08856ce61b71d294630964, contract 0xbd499416061f78beceb10ac00fdecf0232b38208) and Unichain 0x2b6aab1368b9266b585e655377e5a9431b822e4ff4657fec34166824e372a82e. Did the launcher of 0xfd23280b87514ce09dcb47965f1c5465847422eb collect the 34130246063283906 SPCXon credited by factory call 0xf3937729, and do the deployers 0x690193287a9f3e0095adae116f4260818332ce0a, 0x888ddf6a86fd6e6da39395cd3f333ecba55ff364, 0x02dcd01d534477b5e76628a7284e7fa71c7a7ed7 and 0x3a15cf422307e922645d671cb247e76e8b1ec50d, which created second pools on both Ethereum hooks, belong to the hook author or to third parties?
leads.why: The payout step of the finding has been used on Ethereum and three pools with liquidity are frozen because of it. Whether the creator share was withdrawn decides if this was a test by the author or a theft, and a count over all networks gives the realised loss.

leads.question: Who owns the liquidity positions of the Klik launch pools (for example the three frozen SPCXon pools with liquidity 153845604096252485200300 on Ethereum), can the owner remove them, and how much quote currency do the pools of the nine networks hold in total?
leads.why: An ordinary account can raise pendingClaims of any launched token from a pool without liquidity and stop swaps in that token's real pool. If the positions are locked in the factory, the quote currency paid in by buyers stays in the PoolManager with no swap path, and the severity of the finding should be judged on that amount.

leads.question: Run the census of this unit (Transfer logs that name the PoolManager joined with PoolManager logs per transaction) over the whole history of each network with an indexed log source, and list every transaction where the PoolManager's balance of a token falls without a PoolManager log, whatever the recipient.
leads.why: The full history search of this unit sees only burns. The DEAD case on Base was found because 40 percent of the claim is burned. A token that lets a third party move the PoolManager's balance to an ordinary address is visible only in the windows of 0.5 to 30 days.

attempts.answer: The census covers the whole history on Zora, Celo, Elysium, MegaETH, Tempo and HyperEVM and windows of 3 to 60 days on the other 15 networks. It lists every row where the balance falls without a matching pool amount, whatever the recipient. The busy networks still need an indexed source for the whole history.

leads.question: List pooled tokens that have a public function which moves or burns another holder's balance (idle claims, inactivity decay, reflection sweeps, liquidation of dormant accounts), and test with a read-only call from an unrelated address whether the PoolManager is a valid target today.
leads.why: claimIdleTokens of DeadToken on Base is such a function and an ordinary account used it against the PoolManager. Tokens of the same template may exist on other networks, and the PoolManager is idle for any token whose pools see no payout.

attempts.answer: Three pooled tokens beside the Base DeadToken have a public function that removes the balance of an idle holder with the PoolManager as a valid target: Imperium on Polygon (scanAndClean, valid today, no caller balance needed), the DeadToken copy on Polygon (claimIdleTokens, valid today, 1 base unit pooled) and BankToken on Ethereum (reclaimInactive, valid after the inactivity period in the trial at 91 days, 800 base units pooled). None has a market price. No such function was found among the priced tokens.

leads.question: Finish the burn search for the whole history of Base, Robinhood Chain, World Chain and X Layer, the claim mint list of X Layer, and a dense receipt sample for Base and Robinhood Chain.
leads.why: These searches cover recent windows only, and the two networks with the most claim mints (29.7 million and 9.9 million) were sampled with a lighter rule because of endpoint limits.

leads.question: Part (c) of lead L-318: list native takes whose recipient is not the caller. This needs trace_filter or an explorer export of internal transactions of the PoolManager.
leads.why: Native takes leave no log outside Arc. This unit saw them only through wrapper Deposit logs, through traces of sampled claim mints and through Arc's native logs.

leads.question: Which factory or template produced the tokens that grant the helpers 0xd8e11826e82619bf49c58c05f26c8e00b0b64ea4 on Ethereum and 0xa25c886dced0e8fc0129082bf597381ea073c925 on BNB Smart Chain an allowance from the PoolManager, and how many pooled tokens of that template still hold a PoolManager balance?
leads.why: The same selector 0x73ed6b13 removed the PoolManager balance of 12 tokens on Ethereum and 18 on BNB Smart Chain. Live tokens of the template can be listed before they are used.

leads.question: Does the deployed PositionManager offer a way to remove liquidity when the PoolManager cannot pay one of the two tokens, for example by taking that side as an ERC-6909 claim or by clearing it?
leads.why: For the pools of MAGA, MEME, BITCOIN, ELX, SNI and DEAD the token side cannot be paid by take. Core allows mint and clear (src/PoolManager.sol:310-329), and whether ordinary liquidity providers can reach them decides if their other currency is frozen.

leads.question: Record the sSAC payouts on BNB Smart Chain under F-066 and establish how far they go: list every transaction in which the PoolManager pays out sSAC 0x0ae7cd10f94fd16a6f9a29a372708718144c46f8 or sNVB 0x6d6c16a3cbd318f3000e33cfd27662cf00f7e7c1 in a block where the token's rebase log appears, over the whole history, and sum the amounts.
leads.why: The research file cleared this twice and labelled the two rows spoof. Transactions 0xf1c329b6e3e3fa7747c3907e7d449c536977f0e44b79c10db31ff4153b9f098d and 0x27598a81864c463522634ec554d1e69a255353a9d4d6cf7438471a44ebd6ca1e show sync, rebase, settle and take of 2.538 sSAC each by an ordinary account, at epochs 365 and 366. F-066 says the path was unused on BNB Smart Chain. The call enters through lock(bytes) on a second contract, 0x238a358808379702088667322f80ac48bad5e6c4, which calls the taker back and pays it 999,471 base units of sSAC in the same transaction, so a second pool contract with a lock and callback design appears to be used the same way. I did not identify that contract.

attempts.answer: sSAC: 119 payout transactions between blocks 115,986,214 and 135,186,213 among 191 rebase transactions since block 104,200,000, summing to 210.068614 sSAC. The list is in theme-currency-lists.work/raw/ssac_payout_list.json. sNVB was not scanned over the whole history: the endpoint with wide log ranges reached its limit, and the verifier saw no sNVB outflow in the last 1.2 million blocks.

leads.question: Re-read every row the census flagged and the research file explained by a label (393 on BNB Smart Chain, 50 on Polygon, 126 on Arc, 17 on OP Mainnet), with one rule: a row is spoof only when balanceOf(PoolManager) is unchanged by the transfer, and a row is a rebase payout when the amount equals the balance rise since sync. Then run the same census over the whole history for every token whose balance changes without transfers.
leads.why: One of 134 flagged tokens on BNB Smart Chain was a real payout filed as spoof on the strength of the call pattern of the other 132. The census covers 0.5 to 30 days and skips every transaction that holds a pool event, so a capture that sits next to a swap, or that happened before the window, is unseen.

attempts.answer: Every labelled row was re-read. BNB Smart Chain 393: 391 nopool, 2 surplus (nopool means a token that is in no pool and whose balanceOf reverts). Polygon 50: 49 surplus credits and 1 spoof. Arc 126: all balanced by claim burns. OP Mainnet 17 and Arbitrum One 18: fee collection. The whole history census for tokens whose balance changes without transfers was run for sSAC through its rebase logs.

leads.question: Add PUSD 0xc8fb643d18f1e53698cfda5c8fdf0cdc03c1dbec to the list of pooled tokens that reject transfers from the PoolManager today, and test whether a holder of a position in the eight PUSD pools with liquidity can withdraw the other currency through the deployed PositionManager.
leads.why: blackList(PoolManager) has been 1 since block 455,607,037 and transfers from and to the PoolManager revert with the text blacklist. The finding recorded the burn and missed the freeze.

leads.question: Test the claim mints that sit in transactions with a pool event: for a sample per network, compare each mint with the Swap amounts of the receipt, and trace the ones that hold only ModifyLiquidity logs.
leads.why: About nine in ten sampled mint rows were counted as explained because the transaction holds a pool event. On Unichain 4 of 17 such rows that I tested cannot be confirmed from logs.

leads.question: Rank hooks by what they hold. For each network take the 20 hook addresses with the largest ERC-6909 claim balances (from the claim mint logs that theme-unbacked-claims collected, then balanceOf(hook, id)) and the largest token and native balances, and on Arc first group the 194,252 hook addresses by code hash and take the ten largest groups. Include the launch pad hooks that reject a direct initialize and keep fee ledgers: 0x6b1216a40b65c83e9c9e18a562c446697b8cf8ec, 0xe0def4221b9840a610d4e7d55812a79a6431a8ec and 0x3ab88ddc3cf2a012af88b60828edb4553697e5dc on Elysium, CashCatHookV2, PonsV2MemeHook, 0x4eb1976978756bd56802d8162f2271844924e0cc and 0x2c668601193e4a081dd82604785e436aff6a2acc on Robinhood Chain, WonkHook, MinaraFeeHook and 0x4ab0bf61327761fffc5910052d9e0b9a94f960cc on Arc, TaxLaunchHook on X Layer, LaunchHook on Ethereum, and the Base hooks 0x0469a4bd3724dc86c9542f4694c976da13c450c0 and 0x5e320ea6278107968c119942e57d876c5f922acc, whose sources op-stack-eth could not fetch. For each: is the ledger that decides a payout stored under the pool id, or under a token or a currency? Can an ordinary account reach the callbacks with a currency of its choice, through initialize, through a public factory or, for the Doppler hooks, through the Airlock? In which currency is the payout made? Run the callbacks inside an unlock with eth_simulateV1 or debug_traceCall so that the calls after the first take or burn are visible.
leads.why: The Klik finding is confirmed with actor unprivileged: a fee ledger kept per token is paid in the currency of whichever pool calls, and one Ethereum transaction has already used it. It was found among the most used hooks, and it holds tens of dollars. A hook with the same fault and large claims would let an account that opens its own pool take what the hook holds for the pools of other users. No unit ranked hooks by value, the probes ran outside an unlock, and more than nine tenths of the hooked pools on Arc use addresses nobody read.

attempts.answer: Hooks were ranked by holdings on all 21 networks (claims from the cycle 5 mint logs plus the most used currencies, token balances, native balance), the 20 largest per network were probed, sources were read for the largest and for the named launch pad hooks, and open hooks were run inside an unlock through the Quoter with a state override. Two new hook faults came out: three route hooks on Arbitrum One pay any pool from their own balance (about 124 USD), and SpawnerHook on Base shares one ETH fee bucket across tokens (about 1.6 USD pending). The named launch pad hooks with source store their ledgers per pool id or per paid currency. The hooks with large balances (SatoHook 981 ETH, Uniwall 127 ETH of claims, Angstrom, Doppler, Sazare) pin their currencies or reject foreign pools. Unread: the unverified 0xc81fd894 hook with about 1.1 million USD and every Elysium hook. On Arc the 194,252 hooks form 605 groups by size and flags, and the ten largest groups hold about 150 USD together.

leads.question: Build the full currency list of the PoolManager on Base, BNB Smart Chain and World Chain with the log sources theme-shared-hooks used in cycle 5 (base.gateway.tenderly.co in windows of 1,000 blocks, the NodeReal endpoint for BNB Smart Chain, the QuickNode endpoint for World Chain), and on X Layer as far back as the endpoint serves. Rerun xfer_sweep.py, assign_sweep.py and third_sweep.py from theme-assigned-balance.work and the equal balance grouping of established-l1 on the new lists. Which tokens with a price let a third party lock, claw back, sweep or mirror the PoolManager balance?
leads.why: The tested lists hold 9,108 currencies on Base against 15.6 million pools, 3,369 on BNB Smart Chain against 341,033 pools, 851 on World Chain and 96 on X Layer. Base carries the most value after Ethereum, and DEAD, the one token an ordinary account has already emptied, is on Base. This closes L-317 and L-291.

attempts.answer: The four lists are complete from the deployment block: Base 15,315,529 currencies in 15,540,638 pools, BNB Smart Chain 78,255 in 341,903, World Chain 826 in 4,760, X Layer 3,750 in 12,500. The three sweep scripts and the equal balance grouping ran on every new currency with a balance on BNB Smart Chain (68,701), World Chain (7) and X Layer (2,051) and on a Base set of 59,170 currencies that covers every code family. With a price: ibBUSD on BNB Smart Chain can be burned out of the PoolManager by any account (new finding), HOLD is restricted by its issuer (new finding), FACTR and TC accept locked assignments (class of F-078). No mirror pair.

leads.question: For every pooled token with a price and a PoolManager balance above 1,000 USD: call, from an unrelated address, each function of the token that takes an address argument, with the PoolManager as that argument, and record whether balanceOf(PoolManager) falls, whether the full balance can still be sent, and who receives the amount. Run each trial at the current block and again with the block time moved forward by 8 hours and by 400 days (eth_call block override), so that inactivity sweeps, expiries, unlock dates and rebases that are not yet due show up. Include the 52,820 selectors that the signature database could not name. Then list every pooled token on the 21 networks that has the selector of claimIdleTokens(address) or emits the TokensClaimed topic 0xa86305abc2db271df4609aa86a8d044bc11fb36939841bfdad6c1ab2b26e9471.
leads.why: claimIdleTokens of DeadToken on Base moved the whole pooled balance out of the PoolManager after 90 quiet days, half of it to an ordinary account, and the search found it only because part of the amount is burned. A test at the current time cannot see a rule that waits for a date, and the two confirmed findings of theme-assigned-balance came from functions with well known names. A priced token with such a rule is a loss for hookless pools that an ordinary account can cause.

attempts.answer: Done for 2151 priced tokens on 19 networks with all selectors, including 14775 without a known name, at four block times and in a second mode where the PoolManager sends nothing first. No priced token above 1,000 USD lets a stranger lower the PoolManager balance or lock it, apart from QANX (F-078). The selector search for claimIdleTokens and related names on 20 networks found the DeadToken copy on Polygon (1 base unit pooled), Imperium on Polygon (3,029 IMP, can be burned by anyone today, about 1.57 USD of reserves) and BankToken on Ethereum (dust). The TokensClaimed topic was not searched, because the code files of cycle 5 keep four byte constants only. Open: the incomplete currency lists of Base, BNB Smart Chain, X Layer and World Chain, Robinhood Chain for the selector search, and Monad for shifted block times.

leads.question: Repeat the transfer census of theme-unbacked-claims with one rule and no labels. For every transaction in which the PoolManager balance of a token falls, read balanceOf(PoolManager) one block before and at the block. Class the row as spoof only when the balance is unchanged, as a surplus payout when the amount equals the rise of the balance since a sync in the same transaction, and as open otherwise, whatever the recipient and whether or not the transaction holds a Swap or ModifyLiquidity log. Start with the rows that the research file explained by a label (393 on BNB Smart Chain, 50 on Polygon, 126 on Arc, 17 on OP Mainnet), then extend the windows of 0.5 to 30 days to the whole history with an indexed log source. Which rows stay open, and which contract was called between sync and settle in each?
leads.why: This census is the one search of the review that assumes no mechanism, so a capture of pool funds that has already happened on any network would appear in it. The verifier found that two of the 393 BNB Smart Chain rows filed as spoof are real payouts, and that about nine in ten claim mint rows were counted as explained because the transaction holds a pool event. The full history search sees transfers to burn addresses only, and the DEAD claim was found only because 40 percent of it is burned.

attempts.answer: The census ran with one rule on all 21 networks: 17,682,242 transactions, 28,103,882 rows, 3,752 flagged, each read with balances, block logs and, where an endpoint serves one, a trace. Transactions with pool events are included. Classes are in the cleared item. Open rows that remain are the sender charge tokens WHITE, ARGUS and T (new finding) and tokens that moved the balance themselves (F-086). The contract called between sync and settle is the staking contract of sSAC, sLGNS and sATH for the rebase rows and sDAI for the two paid rows on Ethereum.

leads.question: Read the verified source of every pooled token worth more than 10,000 USD at the PoolManager whose function list has lock, vest, cooldown, freeze or escrow words (the cleared list of theme-assigned-balance: sUSDe, sENA, apyUSD, aptUSD, syrupUSDC, syrupUSDT, yUSD, ondo, skl, DPR, AST, RNDR and TITANX on Ethereum, SPA on Arbitrum One, the launch pad tokens with lockPool and vesting data on Base). Does balanceOf count an amount that transfer cannot move, and which contract can create such an amount at an address the caller names: a distributor, an auction, an airdrop, a vesting or staking contract with claimTo, claimFor, release or exit? Start from FOLD 0xe172e9b6cfbeeb5593bdce3f077356fdb33af904, where a transfer from the claim source 0x687cc38d8279df3352b64cf3ec1fe8e033933595 locks the amount at the recipient: check the ten bids that are not exited and whether the owner can name a later claim source.
leads.why: The QANX finding is confirmed: locked units that arrive between sync and settle are credited as a payment, and the caller leaves with the liquid units of the pools. The trial sweep called functions of the token only. The verifier read two sources and found that FOLD, of which the PoolManager holds about 23.8 million, would have been open while its auction ran. A priced token whose lock arrives through a second contract gives an ordinary account the same exchange today, and it adds a gain because the locked amount comes from the caller's own allocation. The other tokens of the list were cleared without a source reading.

attempts.answer: Sources were read for one token of each of 111 selector families behind the 160 tokens above 10,000 USD with lock, vest, cooldown, freeze, escrow, idle, inactive, sweep, reflect or claim words. FOLD: the claim source is set once and cannot be renamed, the auction is over, none of its 310 bids belongs to the PoolManager, and the ten bids that are not exited belong to other addresses. Apart from QANX no token of the list lets an ordinary account create a non transferable amount at another address. ondo, skl, SPA, WLFI, SIERRA, StonkCoin and the fxUSD base pool count such amounts and create them only through a role or through the holder's own call. Five tokens have no verified source and rest on trials.

leads.question: Answer leads L-117 and L-315 from chain data on Robinhood Chain. Read the filter contract and the logs of the filterer account: what does each of the entries identify (a transaction hash, a sender, a contract, any address touched during execution), which account adds them and how soon after the transaction they follow, and do the listed transactions share a touched address? Then test by eth_call and debug_traceCall whether a transaction that calls 0x8366a39cc670b4001a1121b8f6a443a643e40951 touches a listed address when a pool it uses was sent 1 wei, or a zero amount native take, from or to that address by someone else.
leads.why: F-001 records that the filter can fail any exit, including forced ones. If entries follow a rule on touched addresses and the rule can be met by state that an ordinary account leaves in the PoolManager or in a pooled token, that account can make other users' withdrawals fail. Robinhood Chain has 1.17 million pools and no unit has read the filter in five cycles.

attempts.answer: Same answer as L-315, from chain data. 6,234 add logs, 1,493 distinct hashes, 1,491 executed with status 0, one filterer account, entries follow a rule on touched addresses that the client applies to the delayed transaction itself. The listed transactions share the wallet 0x42607b2e4fde22e83822d4a86ddac58d847dc289 in 1,389 cases. A zero amount take or a 1 wei payment by someone else leaves no state that a later PoolManager transaction would touch: take writes transient deltas only and the recipient is not stored. eth_call and eth_estimateGas on the public endpoint do not apply the filter, and debug_traceCall was not needed for a path that stores nothing.

leads.question: List every transaction in which the BNB Smart Chain PoolManager pays out sSAC 0x0ae7cd10f94fd16a6f9a29a372708718144c46f8 or sNVB 0x6d6c16a3cbd318f3000e33cfd27662cf00f7e7c1 in a block where the rebase log of the token appears, over the whole history, and sum the amounts. Who controls the contract 0x0b675fb382e0c986d724fd6cbb51837b3ae30e8a and its sender 0x2d68a551e7c8ecf7312ee083a16e736dce2347d5, and is any payout larger than the rise of the PoolManager balance in that epoch? Then ask the same for the staking tokens of the other Olympus forks on the networks where the PoolManager holds them.
leads.why: F-066 says the path was unused on BNB Smart Chain, and the research file of this cycle cleared it twice. The verifier traced sync, rebase, settle and take of 2.538 sSAC each at epochs 365 and 366. The amount is surplus that no pool records, so the entry belongs under F-066. A payout above the rise would be a loss for pools and would change the class.

leads.question: Close what the claim census left on a negative trace. Search the bytecode of all 765 approved operator and spender addresses for the signature strings of burn and transferFrom and for selectors taken from calldata, and trace each hit with a well formed call. Read the unlockCallback of the unverified routers 0xbc22993a15e16acbf12873f234510d35948f7a59, 0x4531332adecf255c66b5bf6485db73f894ed93d2 and 0xad445acd8e2446c652fb47b2d4c5ee9973b150c9 and of the implementation 0xa62f9b597225779b430024398b70374e8468ce14 on Ethereum, of the 47,585 byte hooks with collectPlatform(bytes32[]) and the implementation 0x6b68d5061329f64a087fc894355cb1eacf2a2321 on Robinhood Chain, and of the 677 byte proxies on Base and Robinhood Chain. Decompile the delegate 0xb0c75276657e80ff04c98a3809dfc39a409a8736: can any handler make the account call PoolManager.burn with 0x82ccba35ad0c7a62230ef8ff337ac67f4cce0ea5 as from? Repeat the claim balance step for BNB Smart Chain with an indexed log source. In each case, which account does the burn or transferFrom name, and who chooses it?
leads.why: transferFrom and burn accept an operator or an allowance without any other check (src/ERC6909.sol:35-48, src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22, src/PoolManager.sol:332-336). The census excluded contracts by a constant search that missed one contract with 120 unlimited allowances, which the verifier then cleared by reading. A contract of this list that lets its caller name the debited account would let an ordinary account burn those claims inside its own unlock and take the tokens. The priced exposure of all approvals is about 44,000 USD.

leads.question: Capture the calldata that the hosted Uniswap interface or its liquidity API proposes for removing a position in a pool whose token refuses transfers from the PoolManager (G$ on Celo position 178, ViciCoin on Polygon position 60652 after the daily allowance is used) and decode the action list. Does it ever use CLEAR_OR_TAKE or MINT_POSITION_FROM_DELTAS, and what does it show when the simulation of TAKE_PAIR fails? Run the exit simulation on one of the eight PUSD pools with liquidity on Arbitrum One. Report the two simulations that are in raw and missing from the research file, exitovr_4217_612.json and exitovr_999_123.json: in the HyperEVM file TAKE_PAIR succeeds although the code of the blocked token was replaced, so say whether the endpoint applied the override or the position held none of that token.
leads.why: The finding of theme-claim-operators is confirmed for calldata built with the published SDK, and neither the researcher nor the verifier captured what the interface sends. On Polygon an ordinary account can bring the block about by using up the shared ViciCoin allowance (F-072). If the interface offers neither sequence, a block on one token locks the other currency of each position for users who cannot build a call by hand.

attempts.answer: HyperEVM part only. The endpoint applied the override: balanceOf on the replaced token reverts on four endpoints. TAKE_PAIR succeeded because position 123 was owed nothing in the blocked token. The pool price was exactly at the position's lower tick, fees in that token were 0 and the PoolManager held 0 of it. The simulation shows nothing about a blocked exit and has to be repeated on a position that holds the token. The interface capture and the Arbitrum, Celo and Polygon parts of the lead are outside this unit.

leads.question: Which ModifyLiquidity logs of each PoolManager name as sender, and which ERC-6909 balances name as owner, an address that executes calls for any caller: Multicall3 0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11, the Across MulticallHandler, the settlement and relay contracts that the cycle 4 shared transaction unit listed, Multicall3From and Memo on Arc, and EIP-7702 accounts whose delegate has a batch function without a caller check? For each hit, is liquidity or a claim balance still there?
leads.why: Positions belong to msg.sender of modifyLiquidity and claims to the address named in mint (src/PoolManager.sol:161 and 322-336). Anything held under an address that forwards calls can be removed by any account inside its own unlock. The claim census of this cycle matched these contracts against operators and spenders and found no harmful match. It did not look at them as owners. After Lagoon the messenger 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000023 on OP Mainnet and Unichain becomes such an address.

leads.question: Finish the caller checks of the deployed PositionManager. From an account that is neither owner nor approved, placed by state override with a stub that calls PoolManager.unlock and then, inside its callback, PositionManager.modifyLiquiditiesWithoutUnlock: do DECREASE_LIQUIDITY and BURN_POSITION for another owner's token revert? Do permit, permitForAll and the Permit2 paths reject a signature that the owner did not make, including for owners that are contracts or delegated accounts, and can a subscriber contract that an owner set block or redirect the removal? What does the 19,965 byte build on HyperEVM and Elysium leave out of the 23,877 byte build, and is the source of the PositionManager on Arc published anywhere?
leads.why: Positions made through the PositionManager belong to that contract inside the PoolManager (src/PoolManager.sol:161), so a gap in its caller checks would let an ordinary account withdraw the liquidity of other users on that network. The critic's check shows that the direct path reverts with NotApproved on HyperEVM, Elysium, Arc and Ethereum. The path that runs while another account holds the lock and the signature paths were not tested on any network, and two networks run a build that nobody has read.

leads.question: At every node release or fork that adds or changes a precompile with a ledger, repeat the inherited caller test on chain: a stub that the PoolManager address calls forwards transfer and balanceOf by DELEGATECALL and by CALLCODE to the token. Do both still revert for B20 tokens, the B20 factory and the Policy Registry on Base, for the first CAS20 tokens on BNB Smart Chain mainnet after 2026-12-08, for the TIP-20 tokens, StablecoinDEX, FeeManager and TIP20ChannelReserve on Tempo, and for CallFrom and the Native Coin Authority on Arc?
leads.why: The PoolManager calls contracts that any account chooses (src/PoolManager.sol:110, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134, src/types/Currency.sol:48). In such a frame msg.sender is the PoolManager, and one check in the node (direct calls only) stops that frame from acting on a token as the PoolManager. The check holds today on Base and, by the critic's test, on pathUSD and OUSD on Tempo, where the PoolManager holds 409,943 OUSD. For CAS20 it rests on a source reading, because no token exists on mainnet yet.

attempts.answer: Repeated for the releases that run today on two of the four networks. DELEGATECALL and CALLCODE of transfer and balanceOf with the PoolManager as inherited caller reverted with DelegateCallNotAllowed for pathUSD on Tempo (tempo/v1.19.0-697ea97) and for two B20 tokens on Base (base/v1.5.6). StablecoinDEX, FeeManager and TIP20ChannelReserve on Tempo, the B20 factory and Policy Registry on Base, the Arc precompiles and CAS20 on BNB Smart Chain mainnet were not run. The lead asks for a repeat at every release and should stay open.

leads.question: For the pooled tokens with the largest PoolManager balances whose balanceOf reads a second contract (an exchange, a vault, a rate provider, an oracle, a staking or reward distributor), trace balanceOf(PoolManager) with debug_traceCall, list the second contracts, and call from an unrelated account each of their public functions that takes no argument or one address. Which raise balanceOf(PoolManager) or pay a pending amount to the PoolManager, and how much is due today? Include the triggers that were not due at the time of the cycle 5 sweep (sKLIMA, sNVB and the five staking tokens with a zero distribute word), vault shares with a deposit for function, and the contract that sends ANTB 0x38dd26788cf2d901e3abf04efe3007d459d0fc53 to the PoolManager when BUTTHOLE is transferred on BNB Smart Chain.
leads.why: The trigger probes of this cycle called 70 functions of the token contract itself and found one new token, TITHE. A rebase, a reward or a claim that is started on another contract, as with USD+ and its exchange, is outside them. The amount is credited to whoever brackets the call with sync and settle (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364). It is surplus that no pool records, so a hit extends F-041.

leads.question: Test the claim mints that sit in transactions with a pool event. For a random sample per network, compare each mint with the Swap amounts and the transfers in of the receipt, and trace the ones that hold only ModifyLiquidity logs, starting with the Unichain transactions that begin 0xe5f63adf9abc and 0x80ad0fb09d46. Does any mint exceed what the swap or the removal produced?
leads.why: About nine in ten sampled claim mint rows were counted as explained because the transaction holds a pool event, and the mint itself was not tested. The verifier checked 12 rows on HyperEVM and 17 on Unichain, and 4 of the Unichain rows cannot be confirmed from logs.

leads.question: Finish the token tests of theme-assigned-balance on Robinhood Chain, Elysium and Arc: the full balance transfer test, the test for a balance that rises on a transfer, and the lock and clawback trials for every distinct code hash on Robinhood Chain in place of the sample of three tokens per code size. Which tokens with a price refuse a full transfer, count units that cannot be sent, or let a third party lower the PoolManager balance?
leads.why: These three networks hold 1.13 million of the 1.24 million pooled currencies and were covered through families and samples. The 2,439 refusals on Robinhood Chain and the 115 on Arc were counted and not looked at.

leads.question: Run the equal balance grouping of established-l1 (balanceOf(PoolManager) for every pooled currency, groups of identical non zero balances, one unit transfer per member) on Ethereum, OP Mainnet, Base, Unichain, Arbitrum One, Monad and HyperEVM. On Ethereum start with the two EURe addresses 0x3231Cb76718CDeF2155FC47b5286d82e6eDA273f and 0x39b8B6385416f4cA36a20319F70D28621895279D and the other Monerium tokens: which pools use each address and how much is owed under each id?
leads.why: The test found a second working address for EURe on Polygon and is complete on two networks only. Ethereum holds 4,188.47 EURe readable at both addresses. Core conserves value per id, so the hazard found so far is an issuer freeze, and a pair in which one address reports in another unit has not been ruled out beyond the 170 most pooled tokens.

attempts.answer: HyperEVM part done at block 52,051,531. 307 ERC-20 currencies, 262 nonzero balances, 14 groups of equal balance with 144 members. 135 one unit transfers changed only the balance of the token sent. Nine members, the strategy tokens of one hook product, revert on any plain transfer from the PoolManager with InvalidTransfer() and sit in nine separate pools. No second address for one balance was found.

leads.question: In the Klik factories (0x20839c453a0ed8bcab1095ea068669469098297c on Tempo, 0xb6da931df2ed2c80db47923d4eb46fd913ee01c3 and 0x95e0da371711502eed78bcc3f17856b4415120ca on Ethereum, and factory() of each other hook): may any account call the launch function on Tempo as on Ethereum, and does collectFees(token) pay creatorFees[token] in pairOf(token) whatever currency the hook credited? Did the launcher of 0xfd23280b87514ce09dcb47965f1c5465847422eb withdraw the 34130246063283906 SPCXon credited in Ethereum transaction 0xd903d0ada1874646896a5191a2ef25accec3c3db1333914542b6ad9a8c96bfed, and do the four deployers that created second pools on both Ethereum hooks belong to the hook author? Repeat the burn trace on Base, Ink, Arbitrum One and Avalanche for a token with pending fees, with all pools of each hook listed from the Initialize logs.
leads.why: The verifier showed that the payout step has run on Ethereum and froze three pools with liquidity. If the factory pays the creator share in the real quote currency, an ordinary launcher turns fees booked in a worthless currency into the factory's balance, which is a direct gain. On four networks only the open initialize was confirmed. The amounts today are tens of dollars.

leads.question: Who owns the liquidity positions of the Klik launch pools, can the owner remove them, how much quote currency do these pools hold on the nine networks, and does the sequence the verifier described (initialize a second pool of token T, mint claims of an own currency to the hook, swap there) stop swaps in the real pool of T when run end to end in eth_simulateV1?
leads.why: The verifier derived that any account can stop swaps in the pool of another creator's token and did not simulate it. If the positions are locked in the factory, the quote currency paid by buyers stays in the PoolManager with no swap path, and the severity should follow that amount.

leads.question: Build the one table of pooled tokens that reject a transfer from the PoolManager today. For the refusals on OP Mainnet (110), Arbitrum One (178, with PUSD 0xc8fb643d18f1e53698cfda5c8fdf0cdc03c1dbec), Polygon (104), Monad (62), World Chain (43), Ink (39), Unichain (37) and Base (27), and for yUSD, yETH, xSolvBTC, KITE and NTX on Ethereum: which have a price, what is the balance worth, since which block does the refusal hold, and is the cause an entry for the PoolManager address, a rule for all contracts, a pause, or a rule the author of the token wrote? Does the YieldFi list name the PoolManager address or a class of addresses?
leads.why: About 1.67 million USD is blocked on Ethereum by five tokens, which the verifier confirmed, and the other networks were counted and not valued. Whether issuers list the singleton address on purpose decides if the same will happen to a new deployment. Two critics and two verifiers have asked for this table.

leads.question: Run the sixteen shape sweep through a forwarding stub at the PoolManager address on Ethereum, Celo, X Layer, Monad and MegaETH, with the target lists of the earlier top level sweeps. Does any target answer differently from the top level call, return 32 bytes that start with a hook selector, or return a 32 byte true to transfer without being a token?
leads.why: This is what remains of lead L-209. Thirteen networks showed no difference. Celo and X Layer have a non ETH gas token with core contracts of their own, and Monad and MegaETH have precompiles that read the caller's position in the call stack.

leads.question: Test assumption A1 on block production with chain data. On each of these networks find a block in which one transaction calls sync with a token address and no settle follows in that transaction, and a later transaction of the same block calls settle or settleFor with msg.value above zero without a sync of its own. Did the later one succeed? Where an endpoint serves eth_simulateV1 or debug_traceCallMany for Monad, World Chain, Celo or Avalanche, also run the two call TSTORE and TLOAD test of the cycle 5 critic.
leads.why: A native settle reverts with NonzeroNativeValue while a token is synced (src/PoolManager.sol:356), so one such pair in a block shows that the synced currency was cleared between transactions by the node that produced the block. Four endpoints refused the simulation, and the producing nodes of HyperEVM and MegaETH are closed.

attempts.answer: No such pair exists in HyperEVM history. All 2,760 transactions with a PoolManager log were traced: none ends with an unconsumed token sync, 85 settle native value without a sync of their own, 55 of those are not first in their block, and in the 6 blocks where an earlier transaction called the PoolManager none left a sync. The official endpoint and the testnet endpoint refuse eth_simulateV1, eth_callMany and debug_traceCallMany. The archive endpoint serves them, which tests the archive client only. Inside one execution the official node rolls back and keeps transient storage as Ethereum does (22 probes), and the deployed PoolManager shows the NonzeroNativeValue guard and its reset by sync(address(0)).

leads.question: On Tempo and Elysium, can any transaction type, system transaction, precompile or parent chain message call a contract of the sender's choice with msg.sender equal to address(0)? For Tempo read which sender the end of block system transactions and the fee manager calls carry and whether their target is fixed. For Elysium read how messages from the parent chain are aliased and whether a parent chain sender can map to address(0).
leads.why: protocolFeeController is address(0) on both networks. A caller with that address passes src/ProtocolFees.sol:36 and 48, can set the protocol fee of every pool to the cap and collect it to any recipient. The other eleven networks without a controller have a cleared item for this question.

leads.question: After Lagoon activates on OP Sepolia and Unichain Sepolia (target 10 December 2026): which implementations sit behind 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000022 to 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000028, do ETHLiquidity, SuperchainETHBridge and SuperchainTokenBridge have a receive or fallback function or any selector the PoolManager can send, and what does each return to the sixteen call shapes?
leads.why: The clearance was read from the develop branch because nothing is deployed. A payable fallback would add a recipient that strands a caller's payout (the shape of F-048), which is a loss for the caller only, so this is a check of a clearance and no path to pool funds is known.

leads.question: Before 2026-12-08: has any pool of the BNB Smart Chain PoolManager been initialized with a currency or hook that starts with 0xCA52 or equals 0x70, 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000002007, 0xCA5F000000000000000000000000000000000000 or one of the two 0x7020 registry addresses (filter the 341,033 Initialize logs through the endpoint the hooks unit used)? After the fork: has GovHub appointed the activation administrator, which CAS20 tokens exist on mainnet, which have pools, and what do their policy ids, pause bits and role holders say?
leads.why: Jenner turns these addresses from accounts without code into native code fifteen days from now. The unit showed that no credit can exist under them today, and a look at the logs confirms that no pool waits there. F-007 becomes live when the first CAS20 token is pooled.

leads.question: Run the upcoming forks angle on the six families that did not get it in cycle 5. For each network: which upgrade is scheduled or announced for the next six months, and does it add a transaction type, a precompile, a predeploy or a token standard that answers transfer, balanceOf, a hook selector or a value call from the PoolManager? For the clients built on go-ethereum, name the fork at which a call from 0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe carries its stated value without a balance transfer (the rule F-058 records on BNB Smart Chain and the cycle 3 reading found switched off on the Nitro chains until Amsterdam rules), and say whether any call from that address can reach a target that an ordinary account chooses.
leads.why: settle credits msg.value without reading a balance (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354). A system caller whose value is reported and not moved is harmless only while every call from it has a fixed target and zero value. That was checked for BNB Smart Chain and nowhere else as a question about the future.

leads.question: Answer the Celo half of lead L-218 from the deployed PositionManager and the first Universal Router: which address do they return as wrapped native, what do the WRAP and UNWRAP actions (21 and 22 in posm_actions.json) do when that address is the CELO token, and how do SWEEP and the pay step treat msg.value when the pool currency is the CELO token and when it is address(0)?
leads.why: 88 pools use the CELO token address and 18 use address(0), and the periphery treats the token, which is the native balance itself, as a wrapper. Core was cleared for the two faces. The periphery that ordinary users go through was not read in five cycles.

leads.question: Settle F-024 with the observation named in lead L-263: read what the per transaction observation limits of the X Layer builder filter count, then look for one mined transaction after 10 November 2026 that exceeds a limit. Does one exist?
leads.why: F-024 has been plausible for five cycles on one fact, whether the filter is switched on for the mainnet sequencer. One transaction above the limit shows it is off.

leads.question: Settle F-020 with one fact: does HyperCore require proof of control (a signature, a CoreWriter action or a deployer match) from the EVM address that an AQAv2 treasury designation names before unsigned transfers leave that address? Look for a designation whose named address is a contract that never called CoreWriter, and for the validator vote or action type that created it.
leads.why: F-020 stays plausible on this rule. If no proof is required, the party that can name the address can move tokens out of a contract that cannot sign, which is the operator hazard the finding describes.

attempts.answer: Privileged actor. No proof of control is visible: the mainnet treasury address has no HyperCore action and the deployer's action carries no address. I found no treasury designation that names a contract. In the linked contract role the node already sends unsigned transfers in the name of contracts on mainnet and testnet. The rule itself is unpublished.

leads.question: Answer the three open items of lead L-313 by reading src/ and by behaviour tests on a deployed PoolManager. For sync without a lock: which network lets code run between another user's token transfer and that user's settle? For take on an address without code: which addresses change from no code to code at a scheduled fork, and can a pool, a claim or a debt exist under them before it? For the functions without noDelegateCall: call unlock, take, settle, mint and burn through DELEGATECALL from a stub and say what an account that points its EIP-7702 delegation at the PoolManager exposes. Then answer L-314: which lines of the custody path would no test in test/ catch if removed, and which network feature of ASSUMPTIONS.md A1 to A14 would each have to hold against?
leads.why: The review is about a build of this checkout, and every chain test of cycles 4 and 5 ran against the contracts deployed today. No unit has read the custody path since cycle 3 and these leads were not assigned twice. The first item of L-313 is answered by the cycle 1 items and by the critic's check that the deployed contracts collect fees inside an unlock.

attempts.answer: The three open items of L-313 are answered by reading and by tests on the 21 deployed PoolManagers. The PoolManager makes no call between a payer transfer and its settle, so code of a third party can run there only if the token or the payer router calls it, and such code would not need sync because settle is open to every caller while the manager is unlocked. This unit did not survey whether the enshrined token standards call out during a transfer. Addresses that turn from codeless to code are the CAS20 range on BNB Smart Chain at the Jenner fork and the B20 and TIP-20 ranges on token creation, and nothing can be owed or held under them before. An account that points its EIP-7702 delegation at the PoolManager exposes its own balances to flash borrowing and to the booking of triggered inflows, and nothing of the PoolManager. The fourth part of the lead, the list of lines that no test pins, belongs to lead L-314 and was left to the unit core-code-test-pins.

leads.question: Which template produced the tokens that grant the helpers 0xd8e11826e82619bf49c58c05f26c8e00b0b64ea4 on Ethereum and 0xa25c886dced0e8fc0129082bf597381ea073c925 on BNB Smart Chain an allowance from the PoolManager through selector 0x73ed6b13, and how many live tokens of it still have a PoolManager balance? What does the implementation 0x89ec479a783ff3747f2f0d3c2a292c5986cec099 behind the PUSD proxy check in burnFrom and in the function with selector 0x85c1e21d? For CLU on Elysium, is the exemption flag read for tx.origin or for msg.sender?
leads.why: The helper selector removed the PoolManager balance of 18 tokens on each of the two networks, and live tokens of the template can be listed before they are used. The victims chose a pool with a token of that author, so this stays outside the unprivileged scope.

leads.question: Settle F-062 with one observation: in a MegaETH block that holds a transaction filling the per block budget for new state, are the transactions after it ordered by arrival or by priority fee, and were later candidates of that block skipped? Use the receipts and the mini block fields of recent blocks.
leads.why: F-062 is plausible because the payload builder is closed and its ordering rule was inferred. The delay it describes exists only if a paying transaction cannot move ahead of the queue.

leads.question: Run the behaviour test of lead L-217 on the Unichain predeploy with a caller contract placed by state override: settle with value after sync of a token reverts with NonzeroNativeValue, settle after sync(address(0)) credits msg.value, take reverts while locked, clear accepts only the exact positive delta, mint and burn move the delta and the claim by the same amount, and collectProtocolFees for a synced token reverts.
leads.why: The predeploy has 24,050 bytes against 24,009 elsewhere, and every Unichain result of five cycles describes it. The test takes one sitting and has been skipped four times.

attempts.answer: Run on 2026-11-24 with PM_FROM=130: the Unichain predeploy bytecode gives the same records as the Ethereum bytecode on all 550 scripts of pmdiff.py and pmdiff2.py, on the Ethereum and the Unichain node, and 400 scripts of pmdiff3.py equal the reference interpreter on both. Set 2 includes settle with value after sync of a token. See opcodes/unichain-predeploy.json.

leads.question: What is TITHE 0x3751b9250a90342e47173bd3a7c7de4f297c060a worth, which pools hold it, and do the three other Robinhood Chain tokens with the same selector set pay rewards to the PoolManager when any account calls claimFor?
leads.why: 10,002.56 TITHE can be booked by any account today, which the verifier confirmed without an override. No price was found, and the amount is surplus that no pool records.

leads.question: On World Chain the trial sweep recorded that an ordinary account which had just received a third of the PoolManager balance gained 1,874,084 units from withdrawDividend() on 0x5b51b28cb3b7d3dfa2463f3df7ce3929c1464f1b and 2,429.9 units from claimDividend() on 0x98b440dc0491e076ab029bf9fc502a5a721ccce1 (raw/assign_480.json.gz, class A-gain). Does the payout scale with the balance held at the time of the call, where does it come from, and does it have a price?
leads.why: If the holder of the moment can claim, any account can borrow the whole pooled balance with take, claim the dividend and settle in one unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297), which is assumption A5. The payout would come from the reward pot of the token and not from pools.

leads.question: Do holders of locked QANX with allowedHops of at least 1 exist on 0xaaa7a10a8ee237ea61e8ac46c50a8db8bcc1baaa and 0xaaa9214f675316182eaa21c85f0ca99160cc3aaa? Read the LockApplied logs and lockOf for the recipients and state how much locked QANX could be sent to the PoolManager with transferLocked.
leads.why: Both contracts let a sender pay a locked transfer from its own locked balance. Such a holder can book locked units between sync and settle and take liquid ones, which turns the freeze of the QANX finding into a gain. The pooled amounts are a few hundred USD.

leads.question: Do routers or interfaces list pools from allPools or getPoolCount of the ERC-4626 wrapper hooks (0xc9987661b047cd73e3b0d66b2b7615a2ca811088 on Polygon, 0x89fcd09773c7c46ea20887c5246033f8a0a1d088 on Arbitrum One, 0x987105e95645d39ad967c8698478e17861271088 on OP Mainnet, 0x8d92ff0a753dbc32e5c9c9f6493a1410d83e1088 on Monad), and what does afterInitialize check about the vault besides asset()?
leads.why: Any account can register a pool for a vault contract it wrote, and a swap through such a pool hands the input to that contract. That harms only users who are routed there, so it matters if a router trusts the list of the hook.

leads.question: Complete the hook census where it is partial: Base blocks 37,000,001 to 49,000,000 were read one window in four, and X Layer was read for the most recent 1.4 million blocks. Which hooks enter the five most used once the gaps are filled, and do they accept a pool from an ordinary account?
leads.why: A widely used hook that created its pools in the unread ranges is missing from the census. The X Layer hook named in lead L-258 created no pool in the window that was read.

leads.question: Do any two pooled currencies share a balance in different units, for example a share token and its underlying read through one ledger, beyond the 170 most pooled tokens per chain? Use a probe contract that returns one changed flag per token so that the cap of 100,000 bytes on return data does not limit the group.
leads.why: The equal balance grouping finds only faces with a one to one unit. A pair in another ratio would let one payment be read under two ids at different amounts, and it was ruled out for 170 tokens per chain only.

leads.question: Which op-reth commit does the OP Mainnet sequencer run, and does revm at the exact version 41.0.0 that op-reth v2.4.2 pins clear transient storage in commit_tx and discard_tx? When Everest gets an activation time on Base, does the Base Transaction executor still require a secp256k1 signature of the sender and of the payer?
leads.why: Two released builds that follow OP Mainnet were read, the block producer is unidentified, and the journal was read on the main branch of revm. The Everest file returns HTTP 404 on the main branch of the Base repository, so the reading of this cycle describes v1.5.6 only.

leads.question: Once interop is live on OP Mainnet and Unichain, do any routers, intent settlers or bridges send tokens or ETH to the PoolManager in one cross-chain message and call settle in a later step or a later message?
leads.why: Relays are permissionless. An account that executes such a relay inside its own unlock, after its own sync, is credited the payment (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364). Core is safe, so this concerns periphery that will be written for the fork.

leads.question: Is the PoolManager address enrolled in a USDG payout group on Robinhood Chain and on Ethereum, as it has been on X Layer since 2026-11-19 (F-073), and which address receives the rewards that accrue for its balance there?
leads.why: The registrar acted on the X Layer PoolManager four days before cycle 4. The same issuer runs USDG on the other two networks, and nobody read the group of the PoolManager there. This is an issuer act and is recorded for reference.

leads.question: Part (c) of lead L-318: list the native takes of each PoolManager whose recipient is not the caller, from trace_filter or an explorer export of internal transactions, and for each recipient that is a contract say what it did with the value and whether the caller's native debt was paid in the same transaction.
leads.why: Native takes leave no log outside Arc, so the census of this cycle saw them only through wrapper Deposit logs and sampled traces. A recipient that books value for the PoolManager or returns it under another currency id would show up here.

leads.question: After each Bor release: does 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001010 still return false for transfer without value and true for a zero amount, and did any genesis contract change code? When the Igloo rule set for the C-Chain is published: does it include ACP-209 with the precompile at 0x0200000000000000000000000000000000000006, which takes value for a named account?
leads.why: Polygon forks reach validators as private builds, and Uburu replaced the code at 0x1001. A version of 0x1010 that moves POL without value would turn the dead credit of F-008 into a second working face of the native asset, with the guard at src/PoolManager.sol:356 as the only protection.

leads.question: Check ArbOwnerPublic.getScheduledUpgrade() on Elysium once per cycle (selector 0x81ef944c at 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000006b). When it returns a version and a time, answer L-001 and L-134 on the testnet first: how are ElysiumCoreWriter callbacks delivered, does the predeploy accept value with empty calldata and credit msg.sender, and does it answer balanceOf or transfer?
leads.why: The call returned zeros on 2026-11-23, so nothing can be read today. A callback that the node runs inside a user's call, or a predeploy that books value to the sender, would touch assumptions A1 and A3 on the network with 131,891 pools.

leads.question: Which accounts hold the operator role and the admin role of Dinari USD+ at 0xfc90518d5136585ba45e34ed5e1d108bd3950cfa, and what does rebaseSub(uint128,bytes32) do in the deployed implementation 0xff5bff8081eaee966bd74e9c0c059949df2345e1, whose source I could not obtain?
