On Arc the same question was answered this cycle: entries come from named denylisters only.

leads.question: Do the parent chain token gateways of Robinhood Chain (on Ethereum) and of Elysium (on HyperEVM) answer the selector of outboundTransferCustomRefundWithSlippageTolerance, and do they name a master vault? If so, which tokens that the PoolManager holds are bridged through it, what is the vault's share price today, and who holds the vault roles?
leads.why: The yield bearing bridge reviewed by Trail of Bits in August 2026 routes every deposit through an ERC-4626 vault once a chain owner deploys it, and a loss in the vault is spread over depositors at withdrawal, which the report records as accepted. Bridged tokens in pools would then be redeemable for less than their face amount. The actor is the chain owner, so this is recorded for reference.

leads.question: What was the lowest base fee on Arc in the last 1,000,000 blocks (eth_feeHistory), which parameter sets the 20 gwei floor, and who can change it? At which gas price does the rounding gain of one settle on the token face (less than 10^12 wei) exceed the cost of the value call that forces the wei in (at least 9,000 gas)?
leads.why: The clearance of the 12 digit truncation rests on the cost of gas and no longer on a missing path, since this cycle showed that a self destruct delivers native value to the PoolManager. The break even price is about 0.11 gwei. The floor is cited from the documentation page and was not read from chain or from the client.

leads.question: Celo, carried for the seventh cycle (L-218 and L-086): with WETH9() of the deployed PositionManager and of the first Universal Router equal to the CELO token 0x471EcE3750Da237f93B8E339c536989b8978a438, simulate through each contract a mint and a full removal on one of the 88 pools that use the CELO token address and on one of the 18 pools that use address(0), with wrap, unwrap, sweep and take actions. Which actions revert, and does any path leave native value or CELO in the contract where the next caller can sweep it?
leads.why: Celo is the one network where the ERC-20 face of the native asset can be paid out by take, and most native liquidity there sits under the face. Ordinary users reach the PoolManager through these two contracts. A path that strands a user's native value in the periphery would be a loss for users who did nothing unusual, and no unit has run it in seven cycles.

leads.question: For each network, take the 200 pooled currencies with the largest priced balance at the PoolManager and measure the gas of transfer(fresh address, 1) from the PoolManager by eth_estimateGas with the from field set. Which tokens need more than 1,000,000 gas, and for which of them does the cost grow with a count that any account can raise (holders, checkpoints, registered recipients, snapshots)? Compare with the gas cap of one transaction on that network.
leads.why: MUPPETS on World Chain needs 4.55 million gas per transfer and 14,143 more per holder, and it stops moving near 1,210 holders under the cap of 16,777,216 gas. That token is in no pool. The same pattern in a pooled token would let any account stop every take of it by creating holders, and no test of earlier cycles recorded gas. op-stack-eth wrote this lead for its seven chains. Every network has a gas cap per transaction or per block, so the question holds for the others too.

leads.question: Does the state lookup of the Monad, MegaETH, Tempo, Arc or HyperEVM client change a storage slot index, a transient slot index or an account address before it reads state, by a rule that maps two inputs to one entry and that needs more than one changed bit (a mask of several bits, a prefix rule, a bucket or page number used as the stored index)? On Avalanche, does the fold of bit 248 also apply to the slot indexes that eth_getProof and state sync report?
leads.why: The one-bit probe of this cycle found the Avalanche fold of bit 248 and nothing else, and it cannot see a rule that needs two or more bits. The PoolManager keeps every pool, position and claim in slots derived by keccak256 (src/libraries/Pool.sol:83-91, src/ERC6909.sol:15-19) and the lock, deltas and synced currency in four constants and hashed transient slots (src/libraries/Lock.sol:8, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:10-16). A lossy rule in a client would let one account's slot stand in for another's. Client source is the only way to rule it out.

leads.question: On the 14 networks where eth_simulateV1 was refused, missing, or no claim holder was found in the log window, does a transfer or transferFrom of an ERC-6909 claim from a holder to itself leave balanceOf unchanged on the deployed PoolManager? Use debug_traceCall with a state diff where the endpoint allows it, or the forwarder stub of cycle 6.
leads.why: Sender equal to receiver is the one input for which two separately computed storage slots of src coincide at run time (src/ERC6909.sol:25-48), which is the shape the Solidity bug SOL-2026-7 needs. The seven tested networks include both bytecode variants and behave as the source says, so a different answer is unlikely. The check closes the remaining endpoints for leads L-028 and L-151 without a compiler.

leads.question: Run the rollback probe of this unit (and the scripts of OPCODES.md) against bytecode compiled from this checkout, placed by state override, once a solc 0.8.26 with via_ir is available.
leads.why: Every on-chain test so far ran the bytecode deployed today, so a change in src/ that only shows in a build of this checkout would not have been seen by any probe.

leads.question: On BNB Smart Chain the face sweep lists four tokens (0x026c...ffff, 0x489c...ffff, 0xa5b9...ffff, 0xd270...ffff) whose transfer out of the PoolManager raises the PoolManager's balance of 0x7c8d5502b544ddaf8852fc46d1174e34876d545c. Who owns that inflow, and is any of it owed to a user.

leads.question: Which of the 67 historic failed state syncs that remain replayable under failedStateSyncsRoot of the StateReceiver (leafCount 76, replayCount 9) carry FxChild as receiver, the Ethereum timelock 0x1a9c8182c09f50c8318d769245bea52c32be35bc as sender and the PoolManager owner 0x8a1b966ac46f42275860f905dbc75efbfdc12374 as target, and does that contract execute a message a second time or out of order?

A governance message that failed years ago, for example a change of an owner or a fee setter, would then run as PoolManager owner today (src/ProtocolFees.sol:29-32). The author of the message is governance, so this extends F-010 and is outside the unprivileged scope unless such a leaf exists.

leads.question: Can an ordinary account get a transaction accepted by consensus that core.ApplyTransaction rejects at execution time, for example a sender that holds code by then, so that the executor of every node stops with errFatal (saexec/execution.go line 363, worstcase/state.go lines 202 to 209)?

leads.question: What is the measured gas of one tick crossing and of one empty bitmap word in Pool.swap on the three deployed PoolManagers, taken from Quoter results on a pool whose initialized ticks are counted from the bitmap through StateView?

attempts.answer: Measured through the deployed Quoters at blocks 135,446,931, 97,873,763 and 101,248,950, with the simulated output equal to the Quoter output on every served quote: about 17,000 gas per initialized crossing and 5,600 per empty word on BNB Smart Chain, about 27,700 and 9,200 on Polygon, and 27,000 to 33,000 and 4,900 to 6,400 on Avalanche. The bound of F-111 becomes about 983 crossings per transaction on BNB Smart Chain, about 1,210 on Polygon and about 2,400 to 2,950 per block on Avalanche. F-111 is restated with the measured figures.

leads.question: Repeat the 393 flagged rows of cycle 5 and the Initialize census of 78,255 currencies on BNB Smart Chain with the NodeReal endpoint in 50,000 block ranges, and check each token's result against archive balances as was done for sNVB in cycle 8. leads.question: Robinhood Chain part of lead L-372: replay mined transactions of the 47,585 byte hooks with collectPlatform(bytes32[]) and of the implementation 0x6b68d5061329f64a087fc894355cb1eacf2a2321 from the original sender and from an unrelated account with a call tracer, and read which account each burn or transferFrom into the PoolManager names.

leads.question: The stored one third transfer sweep of cycle 5 lists six Polygon currencies (0x2b0eff3a4464a758e65144edc40f50148a9c3f31 at 97.9 percent, 0x8ef2f93b3c99050fdbd926d30e537997faf32ee0 at 3 percent, 0xe03d6d9e54a0e6d949081b657324febf893ca414 and 0x60a98ec0e146f7f7029e244a3337e300eab53aef at 1 percent, 0x0e2d757d7344ce493f9d30b3e7f2ad8017f6dd2b at 0.5 percent, 0x578991ece5745983a2168ead2e1731383e83147a at 0.22 percent) and one Arbitrum One currency (0xdd7389635d76b921d48158e06ba94df528eca1df at 5.7 percent) whose transfer lowers the PoolManager balance by more than the amount. Do they still do so, what do the pools hold, and is the charge the same for an ordinary sender?

leads.question: In the v0.16.5 x86 emitter of Monad, which instructions does the compiler emit inline and which does it hand to the runtime's shared uint256 library: LT, GT, SLT, SGT, EQ and ISZERO as deferred comparisons fused into JUMPI, and SDIV, SMOD, MULMOD, ADDMOD, SIGNEXTEND and BYTE with non-literal operands? attempts.answer: Inline in v0.16.5: comparisons as cmp and sbb with deferred flags, SIGNEXTEND by a literal index, BYTE, shifts and the literal special cases. Library calls: SDIV, SMOD, DIV, MOD, ADDMOD and MULMOD with non-literal or non power of two divisors, through the same runtime functions the interpreter calls. The inline paths were transcribed and matched the specification in 1,926,792 cases at the edges asked for. MUL and EXP code generation remain unread and are carried as a new lead.

leads.question: Transcribe the v0.16.5 x86 code generation for MUL with one literal operand (mul_optimized and its MulEmitter cases) and run it for the 19 multipliers of TickMath.getSqrtPriceAtTick (src/libraries/TickMath.sol:82-100), the first-step select at TickMath.sol:80, the signed multiply by 255738958999603826347141 at TickMath.sol:225, and mul(r, r) with the same operand at TickMath.sol:142-220, over every intermediate price the whole tick range produces. leads.question: Under the per call frame budgets of https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/megaevm/resource-limits.md, how many initialized tick crossings can one swap make before the PoolManager frame, called from a router at depth 1 or 2, exceeds its KV-update or data-size share and reverts with MegaLimitExceeded? Measure with eth_call through a router on a pool with many dust ticks, and check whether modifyLiquidity to remove a position can hit the same limit.
leads.why: A frame budget that is a fraction of the parent's remaining budget does not scale with the gas the caller supplies. If an ordinary account can plant enough initialized ticks to push a victim's swap or removal over that share, it blocks the operation at no gas price, which is a freeze lever F-042, F-105 and F-111 did not test.

attempts.answer: State growth binds first: about 490 upward crossings of freshly planted ticks at depth 1. KV updates and data size stay far below their shares within the 200 million compute gas limit. The breach reverts the frame as a whole, and the swap can continue in a later transaction. This is a delay without loss and was not measured by eth_call.

leads.question: Monad serves debug_traceTransaction with callTracer and withLog (queried 2026-11-24 on https://rpc.monad.xyz, block 0x7736952), and its docs say it has no opcode level struct logs (https://docs.monad.xyz/reference/json-rpc/overview.md). If it re-executes, apply frames.py of theme-megaeth-executor to mined Monad PoolManager transactions that call sync, settle, settleFor, take, mint or burn, or that hold a reverted unlock frame followed by a completed unlock, and compare receipt status and logs with the trace. A compiled fault in TSTORE rollback, CALLVALUE or return data handling on the settlement path (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364) would credit a payer who did not pay, which is theft by an ordinary account from every pool of that currency. Nothing so far tests this path in blocks.

The task's fallback compares receipts with eth_call at the parent block for transactions at index 0, but on Monad index 0 is always the staking system call. The comparison was therefore run on the first user transaction, at index 1, replaying with debug_traceCall at the parent block with the access list. 2,400 transactions were compared: 1,984 with sync, 2,372 with settle, 2,400 with take, 1 with mint and 285 with a reverted frame that had entered unlock followed by a completed unlock. They hold 287,515 frames. No first divergence belongs to the PoolManager, and 22,893 of 22,930 paired PoolManager frames are identical. The other 37 follow an earlier divergence from a token's balance or the staking precompile. On the recorded frames alone, 12,000 transactions were checked against the source's settlement rules with no mismatch, and all 13,635 completed unlocks without hooks net to zero.

leads.question: Transcribe the Monad v0.16.5 x86 code generation and runtime helpers for RETURNDATASIZE, RETURNDATACOPY, CALLVALUE, TLOAD, TSTORE, KECCAK256 and SIGNEXTEND with a variable index, at each operand location the emitter distinguishes, and run them on the exact instruction sequences of Currency.transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:60-75), balanceOfSelf (src/types/Currency.sol:90-95), CurrencyDelta (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39) and _settle (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364) as they appear in build/PoolManager.json. Their transcriptions match the specification at every operand location: 411,200 CALLDATALOAD cases, 896,400 SIGNEXTEND cases with a variable index, and 159,098 cases for the context readers. Planted faults are caught. The built runtime has no SIGNEXTEND with a variable index. KECCAK256, TLOAD, TSTORE, CALLDATACOPY, RETURNDATACOPY with its bounds check, MCOPY, CALL and STATICCALL call the same C++ runtime functions as the interpreter, and the compiled call glue passes operands in parameter order with interpreter-compatible result aliasing. leads.question: In bor v2.11.1, Call reads the code of the callee twice for an EIP-7702 delegated account: resolveCode calls GetCode(addr) and then GetCode(target), and resolveCodeHash calls GetCode(addr) again and then GetCodeHash(target) (core/vm/evm.go lines 363-370 and 721-748, fetched by the critic). The resulting pair (hash, code) keys the per-block JUMPDEST bitmap in a sync.Map that BlockSTM workers and the prefetcher share (core/vm/jumpdests.go lines 54-78, core/blockchain.go lines 1268-1287, contract.go isCode). Under BlockSTM V2, can the two GetCode(addr) reads of one incarnation return different versions when a lower-index transaction of the same block changes the account's delegation, and is the stored bitmap discarded when that incarnation is later invalidated? Answer from core/blockstm and the ParallelStateDB read path, then test in a dev chain or by reading whether any code path snapshots the account once per call.
leads.why: An ordinary account can redelegate its EOA several times in one block with type 4 transactions, for example first to a contract Y and then to the PoolManager address. A worker that read Y's code and then the PoolManager's code hash would store Y's bitmap under the PoolManager's hash for the rest of the block. validJumpdest checks the byte against the real code but takes code-or-data from the bitmap (contract.go lines 65-80, 86-110), so a Y built from PUSH32 runs marks every JUMPDEST of the PoolManager as data and every PoolManager call in that block reverts on that node. Repeated each block this freezes all Polygon pools for as long as the attacker pays, and a node whose cache differs from the producer's computes another state root for the same block. This is the one lever found on an opcode-path cache that an unprivileged account controls.

attempts.answer: bor v2.11.1 cannot pair one bytecode's JUMPDEST bitmap with another code hash. V2 workers read code through ParallelStateDB, whose readCodeKey caches the first CodePath read of each address for the whole incarnation, explicitly so that resolveCode and resolveCodeHash follow one delegation target (core/state/parallel_statedb.go lines 359-381). The hash it returns is keccak256 of the bytes read, or the parent trie hash of parent-state bytes. A redelegating attacker can at most leave behind a bitmap from a speculative incarnation, and that bitmap is the correct one for the bytes whose hash keys it. The prefetcher, the serial processor, the witness path and the producer use single-threaded StateDBs or per-EVM maps. No transaction ordering and no producer role changes this. The 29 push-data 0x5b bytes of the PoolManager are not named by any push constant, so even a wrong bitmap could not redirect a jump.

The first write in a frame copies the object under the frame's version (version_stack.hpp current(), state.cpp lines 73-86), and a failed frame pops that copy for every address the frame touched (state.cpp pop_reject lines 155-181, version_stack.hpp pop_reject). So nothing a frame wrote survives its revert on either path: a CurrencyDelta or reserves word set by TSTORE inside a reverted frame is gone together with the token transfer. The developers' comment describes what happens inside a frame that is about to fail: compiled code checks gas once per basic block, so it stops before the block, while the interpreter stops part way through it. leads.question: Tempo mainnet now runs tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748 with evm2 35aa3280 (was 66687c18) and reth 167933d1. Read the evm2 diff 66687c18..35aa3280 in the instruction handlers (arithmetic, MULMOD/ADDMOD, shifts, SIGNEXTEND, BYTE, EXP, comparisons), jump destination analysis, memory and MCOPY, call input and output borrowing, return data, and the TSTORE/TLOAD journal and rollback. Say whether Host::execute_call (commit 2bc0eebb, L-632) lets any precompile or system path start a frame from outside a running call. Then rerun battery.py, targeted.py, callsem.py, statekeys.py, pmdiff.py and pmdiff2.py on the v1.19.1 endpoint. Also check whether the release image is built with the opt-in jit feature: bin/tempo/Cargo.toml line 155 lists default features without jit, and line 268 defines jit = tempo-evm/jit; read the Dockerfile and the release workflow at the tag.
leads.why: A live network changed its interpreter after the cycle's checks. A wrong handler or journal result would change FullMath.mulDiv, TickMath or the transient delta rollback (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39) in every Tempo pool, and any user could trigger it.

attempts.answer: Own check after the cycle. The evm2 change 66687c18..35aa3280 was read file by file: no arithmetic, comparison, shift, jump analysis, memory, MCOPY, return data or transient storage handler changed. Host::execute_call (interpreter/instructions/system.rs) lets a precompile start a call with the opcode's charges and goes through the same execute_message as CALL. InterpreterPool::trim (interpreter/runtime.rs) clears the memory of idle pooled frames when no frame is running (evm/mod.rs execute_message, current_frame is None); a running frame is popped out of the pool, the last pooled frame is spared, and a returned frame's output is copied in finish_call_message_run before anything else runs. The SSTORE skip of a cold load now compares with the full cold cost, which gives the same out-of-gas outcome. Release binaries and the Docker image are built with features asm-keccak, jemalloc, otlp (plus default keccak-cache-global), without jit. Reruns on the v1.19.1 endpoint: battery 99,985 of 99,985, targeted 85,544 of 85,544, callsem 50 of 50, statekeys no alias in 12,198 reads, pmdiff 240 of 250 and pmdiff2 294 of 300 with the same differing ids as recorded, pmdiff3 300 of 300. The reth change 31d05e14..167933d1 (337 files) was read for the execution path: crates/engine/execution-cache, the payload processor, prewarming, transaction reuse and the block executor change only in tests, a configurable thread count and a log line; bal_path_eligible returns the same decision with a reason string. The engine tree module was split into several files (canonical, forkchoice, insert, persist, sync) and that chain-tracking code was not read line by line. Still open in this lead: the step traces on v1.19.1, which are running, and the engine tree refactor.

gaps.note: MegaETH. The high-throughput unit cleared MegaETH on the statement that every arithmetic and jump instruction of mega-evm is the stock revm one, and on eth_call reruns. That covers the replica and RPC path only. MegaETH states that it uses just-in-time compilation to native code (https://www.megaeth.com/about, fetched 2026-11-24, section Bytecode Compilation), and megaeth-labs publishes an AOT compiler prototype that turns EVM bytecode into C++ that calls evmone opcode handlers on the intx library, with PUSH;JUMP and PUSH;JUMPI fused into super-instructions and per-block gas checks (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/evmone-compiler/master/README.md and lib/compiler/aot_compiler.hpp lines 10-98, fetched 2026-11-24). No cycle has asked which executor produces MegaETH blocks. The 5,833 and 39,074 mined swaps are the only evidence for that path, and they reach only the swap code at common values. This is the same blind spot that OPCODES.md records for Monad, with a different integer library (intx, not ruint) and no published source for the production build.

Monad. The cleared item of high-throughput for lead L-575 says the build has no MULMOD with a literal power of two modulus and that the battery therefore tests the code the blocks run. Its verifier found two such MULMODs (pc 22378 with modulus 2^128 from Position.sol:94 and 96 via FullMath.sol:48, and pc 22639 with modulus 2^96 from SqrtPriceMath.sol:240 and 250 via FullMath.sol:48) that compile to inline x86 through mul_mod2, mul_with_bit_size and MulEmitter, which no eth_call reaches and no mined swap has run. The clearance of L-575 is therefore incomplete for those two sites, and the MUL code generation that OPCODES.md lists as not read is still not read. The verifier's bound on the error rests on reading only.

Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche. The arbitrum-family unit raised Go issue 81863 (a dead store pass that ignores a CondSelect of two local addresses and silently drops a store) for nitro built with go1.27.3. The same fault applies to the Go 1.26 line, which was fixed in go1.26.11 on 2026-11-10 (https://go.dev/doc/devel/release, fetched 2026-11-24; fix diff at https://go.googlesource.com/go/+/00ba484%5E%21/ adds OpCondSelect to the deadstore keep rule). Critic queries of web3_clientVersion on 2026-11-24 returned bor/ebcfea01452d and bor/280514fa9fb7 v2.11.1-private go1.26.10 (https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com), Geth/v1.8.2 go1.26.10 (https://bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org) and avalanchego/1.15.3 go=1.26.10 (https://api.avax.network/ext/bc/C/rpc). established-l1 did not consider the Go toolchain of these three clients. The battery passed on these very binaries, so only paths the vectors do not reach remain open.

Tempo, Arc, HyperEVM. These are three of the single-client networks that OPCODES.md asks to retest after every release, and none had a unit in cycle 9. Open since earlier cycles: the per-CPU jump destination scan of evm2 and the jit feature on Tempo validators (L-582, L-286); the commit behind arc/v1, which the Arc endpoint still reports on 2026-11-24; the closed HyperEVM validator (the endpoint reports only 'hyperliquid evm Mainnet'). Tempo still reports tempo/v1.19.0-697ea97, so the step trace comparison of OPCODES.md still applies to the endpoint build.

Ethereum and the OP Stack reth networks had no network unit in cycle 9. Lead L-583 can be partly settled: crates.io (https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/ruint/versions, fetched 2026-11-24) lists no ruint release after 1.21.1 of 2026-10-23, and 1.21.0 stays yanked. OP Mainnet answered with op-reth/v2.8.1-72207294 and twice with op-reth/v0.0.0-dev-unknown, so one backend of https://mainnet.optimism.io reports no version, and which ruint it links is not known.

MegaETH. The status of Rex6 stays unsettled: the Rex6 page says it is not scheduled on any network, while the mega-evm v1.7.3 changelog says it was scheduled on mainnet and testnet. The per call frame budgets of the resource limits spec (https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/megaevm/resource-limits.md, fetched 2026-11-24: each inner frame gets a fraction of its parent's remaining compute gas, data size, KV updates and state growth, and a frame that exceeds it reverts with MegaLimitExceeded) were never checked against the number of storage writes a PoolManager frame makes in a swap that crosses many ticks.

gaps.note: Monad. Cycle 10 settled the compiled multiplication paths by transcription (theme-monad-compiled-mul), but the compiled code that decides settlement is still unread and untested: RETURNDATASIZE and RETURNDATACOPY after the balanceOf STATICCALL of Currency.balanceOfSelf (src/types/Currency.sol:90-95) and after the transfer CALL (src/types/Currency.sol:60-75), CALLVALUE in _settle (src/PoolManager.sol:352-356), TLOAD and TSTORE of CurrencyReserves and CurrencyDelta (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39), the KECCAK256 runtime helper that forms every delta slot, and SIGNEXTEND with a variable index. Simulated calls on Monad always use the interpreter (OPCODES.md:111), so the 550 scripts and the 185,529 vectors say nothing about these compiled paths, and mined evidence on Monad covers only Swap events. No unit has compared a mined Monad receipt with an independent re-execution, which the MegaETH unit did for 7,627 transactions.

HyperEVM. Lead L-547 lists HyperEVM, and the hyperevm unit did not answer it: no mined transaction with a reverted unlock frame followed by a completed unlock was checked against re-execution. The cleared item 'Step trace of the archive client' rests on the statement that the archive client verifies headers against the validator's blocks, so a divergence would have stopped it. No source for that statement was fetched. The nanoreth README (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/master/README.md, fetched 2026-11-24) says system transactions arrive from hl-node unsigned and that nanoreth fabricates their signatures, which shows it ingests the validator's block data; it does not say that nanoreth compares its own state root or receipts root with the validator's header.

MegaETH. The finding of theme-megaeth-executor shows the block producer is a closed JIT executor and RPC replicas apply its results without re-execution. The evidence for that executor is 53,811 Swap events, 2,885 replays and 7,627 receipts compared by logs and status. Liquidity removals, fee collections, ERC-6909 burns and any sync, settle or take inside a reverted frame were not observed. The public stateless validator, the only public re-execution that compares full post-state, was not run (the unit's own medium lead).

All 21 networks. Mined evidence is limited to Swap events. ModifyLiquidity events carry no amounts (OPCODES.md:202), so the amounts that block production paid to liquidity providers who removed liquidity or collected fees (Pool.modifyLiquidity, Position.update at src/libraries/Position.sol:94-96, SqrtPriceMath.getAmount0Delta and getAmount1Delta) have never been checked on any network. On Monad, MegaETH and HyperEVM, where block execution runs a path that eth_call does not, this is the withdrawal path of the victims the review protects, and it is checked only by simulated calls.

Keccak cache in front of KECCAK256. stablecoin-l1 found that Tempo and Arc route KECCAK256 through the alloy-primitives process-wide cache (feature keccak-cache-global, fixed-cache 0.1.10 and 0.1.8) and read it for Tempo and Arc only. The op-reth v2.9.0 lockfile also pins alloy-primitives 1.7.3 with fixed-cache 0.1.10 as a dependency (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-reth/v2.9.0/rust/Cargo.lock, fetched 2026-11-24, lines 635-646 and 5259-5260), and the Base v1.5.6 lockfile pins fixed-cache 0.1.10 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/Cargo.lock, line 9775). Whether these binaries turn the global cache on was not read. Polygon's separate 64 byte cache was read in cycle 8.

Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium. Cycle 10 covered these networks only through the Go toolchain theme. The release the endpoints report, nitro v3.13.0-rc.9, is still not public, Elysium's build names no version, and L-547 and L-617 for Elysium remain open.

Celo, X Layer, Ethereum and Avalanche had no network unit in cycle 10 apart from the Go theme for Avalanche. X Layer pins ruint 1.18.0 (OPCODES.md:132), the oldest of the reth based nodes, and is inside the range of advisory RUSTSEC-2026-0220 that theme-megaeth-executor cleared for MegaETH's revm v112 only. Celo's endpoint serves two clients and L-604 (celo-kona moving to revm-interpreter 42.0.0) is unanswered.

Unichain. The op-stack-eth verifier compared the deployed bytecode of six of the seven OP chains with Ethereum. The seventh, Unichain's 24,050 byte genesis predeploy at 0x1f98400000000000000000000000000000000004, has different bytes and has still never run any of the 550 scripts (L-584, L-426 open since cycle 8).

Polygon. Block producers run BlockSTM parallel execution, while the RPC answers eth_call serially. The cycle 3 clearance of transient storage under Bor's parallel executor rests on reading. The receipt against re-execution method of theme-megaeth-executor (frames.py) has not been applied to Polygon.

gaps.note: Elysium and Robinhood Chain. The arbitrum-family cleared item for 99901 says Elysium's unnamed build computed what the official replay accepts. Its verifier disagreed: rollup 0x508C173dFe5F737B3493195Bf785d71fA76fD217 returns validatorWhitelistDisabled() = 0 and one whitelisted validator, 0x8e87f7c65750c25c6708de33823124cf457676b2, an EOA that sent the confirming transaction itself, and the Robinhood rollup 0x23a19d23e89166adedbdcb432518ab01e4272d94 has two whitelisted validators. On those two chains the assertion match shows that the operator's own validator agreed with the operator's node. It is not an independent replay. Only Arbitrum One (whitelist disabled) has the independent check. The cleared item for 99901 should be reworded before it goes into state/cleared.json, and L-617 and L-631 stay open for Elysium.

Polygon. Every endpoint used in cycles 9 to 11 reports a build named v2.11.1-private. On 2026-11-24 polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com answered web3_clientVersion with bor/cb3d19c5f690/v2.11.1-private/linux-amd64/go1.26.10 (critic query), the same as the theme-keccak-cache reading, while theme-closed-producers recorded bor/f2a2d63e69f6/v2.11.1-private on the same endpoint. The v2.11.1 tag sets VersionMeta to an empty string (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/params/version.go lines 26-29, fetched by the critic) and its Makefile adds only GitCommit through ldflags (Makefile line 21), so the -private suffix and the two commits come from builds that the public tag does not describe. The BlockSTM, jump destination and keccak cache readings of cycle 11 were all taken from the public tag. The networks.json endpoint polygon.drpc.org reports Geth/v10.0.0/drpc, which names no client at all.

Twelve networks had no network unit in cycle 11, and the battery, targeted set and script reruns were done only for 42161, 4663, 99901, 42220 and 196. Client versions on 2026-11-24 (critic query of web3_clientVersion on all 21 endpoints in state/networks.json): OP Mainnet now answers op-reth/v0.0.0-dev-unknown/x86_64-linux, an unversioned development build, so neither the op-reth v2.8.1 reading nor the keccak cache reading of theme-keccak-cache is known to apply to it; Arc still answers arc/v1 with no commit; Monad answers Monad/unknown, so which release block producers run (v0.16.5, or v0.16.6 with its new compiled shift path) is not established by any unit.

Monad. theme-monad-settlement-path cleared the compiled settlement opcodes by transcription and by recorded frames, but its own last lead says nobody knows whether v0.16.5 compiles the 24,009 byte PoolManager at all (the native size bound of 10,240 + 32 x 24,009 bytes in compiler/ir/x86.hpp, with a fallback to the interpreter in vm.cpp 157-162). If the PoolManager is never compiled, the 12,000 recorded transactions and the 13,635 net-zero unlocks are interpreter evidence and the transcriptions are the only evidence for a compiled path that a later release or a hot token or router could still take. The monad-rpc reading of debug_traceTransaction is from monad-bft master, not from the release rpc.monad.xyz runs.

Monad, mined liquidity. The theme-mined-liquidity verifier found the native leg count in the Monad cleared item wrong (108 legs, of which only part were attributable from single-transaction blocks) and raised a lead for 21 native legs in shared blocks whose balance difference was not attributed. The cleared text should carry the corrected count before it enters state/cleared.json.

MegaETH and HyperEVM. theme-closed-producers compared receipts with re-execution on public replicas. On MegaETH the public replica applies the sequencer's results, so the trace is a second execution by stock revm and the storage comparison (eth_getStorageAt against prestateTracer) compares two views served by the same replica. The stateless validator, which checks the header commitment, was not run in cycle 10 or 11. On HyperEVM no public client checks the storage that the validator writes (finding 0 of the unit), so a validator storage fault that leaves gas, status and logs unchanged has no public check at all.

BNB Smart Chain has a second client, reth-bsc v0.1.4 (bsc-rpc.publicnode.com, recorded in cycle 9), built on revm. theme-keccak-cache read the keccak cache for geth-family BSC only, and the RUSTSEC-2026-0220 and ruint 1.21.0 readings never covered reth-bsc. Its alloy-primitives, fixed-cache, ruint and revm-interpreter versions and its feature set are unread, and no unit established what share of BSC validators run it.

All networks. OPCODES.md lists 4.4 percent of the bytecode never executed by any script (the error wrapper for a failed call with long return data, a hook call path, mulDivRoundingUp on an output above 2^160) and 129 conditional jumps taken one way and 3 never taken. No unit since cycle 9 has tried to reach them, so these instructions have no network evidence on any of the 21 networks, including the five where block production runs a path that eth_call does not.

gaps.note: Tempo changed interpreter during the cycle. The critic queried web3_clientVersion at https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz on 2026-11-24 and got tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748, while stablecoin-l1 recorded tempo/v1.19.0-697ea97 as the running and newest release. The v1.19.1 lock (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/tempo/v1.19.1/Cargo.lock, compared with the v1.19.0 lock) moves evm2 and all evm2-jit crates from 66687c18 to 35aa3280, reth from 31d05e14 to 167933d1 and reth-core from 275ce4cf to 5dabd396; ruint stays at 1.21.1. The changelog page https://tempo.com/developers/docs/changelog.md still lists v1.19.0 as the newest release and has no v1.19.1 entry, and the repository has no CHANGELOG.md at the v1.19.1 tag (404). Every Tempo vector, callsem, statekeys and pmdiff result of cycle 13 therefore describes a build the endpoint no longer runs, and the evm2 diff 66687c18..35aa3280 was named in L-632 but never read.

Unichain, Ink and Soneium now answer op-reth/v2.10.0-rc.4-65e80332 (critic query of the endpoints in state/networks.json on 2026-11-24). No cycle has recorded rc.4 or commit 65e80332; cycle 12 read rc.1. The lock at 65e80332 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/65e80332/rust/Cargo.lock) pins the same revm 43.0.3, revm-interpreter 43.0.2, op-revm 20.0.0, ruint 1.20.0 and alloy-primitives 1.7.3 as rc.1, so the opcode handlers are probably the same. The reth engine, execution cache and prewarm code between rc.1 and rc.4 was not read, and the battery was not rerun on rc.4.

Fourteen networks had no network unit in cycle 13. On them the only new evidence is the mined-swap replay of theme-swap-residuals, plus the HyperEVM replays of theme-mined-branches. battery.py, targeted.py, callsem.py, statekeys.py and pmdiff.py were not rerun, and no release note since cycle 12 was read for reth v2.11.0, base v1.5.6 (reth v2.5.2), world-chain v2.8.2, conduit-op-reth v2.5.1, celo reth v2.2.0-74cc8bb, xlayer v0.0.7, nitro, bor, BSC geth v1.8.2, avalanchego 1.15.3 or HyperEVM. The Polygon endpoint in state/networks.json (https://polygon.drpc.org) now answers Geth/v10.0.0/drpc, which hides the bor build. https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com answers bor/f2a2d63e69f6/v2.11.1-private (critic queries, 2026-11-24). An eth_call result from the drpc endpoint therefore cannot be tied to a release.

Arc's three public endpoints report three builds: arc_getVersion v0.8.6-rc1 (37812c61) on rpc.mainnet.arc.io (critic query repeated 2026-11-24), v0.8.5 on publicnode and v0.8.6 (8e8edb7a) on dRPC (stablecoin-l1). The opcode battery and pmdiff ran only on the official endpoint. The validator set is permissioned, and no unit established which release the validators run. The v0.8.0 to v0.8.4 stale-cache fault shows that Arc releases differ in state results, so this is more than bookkeeping.

high-throughput's L-674 clearance (eth_call runs on a separate InterpreterOnly VM, monad_executor.cpp 1306-1309 at v0.16.7) means that all 185,529 vectors and the 550 to 706 pmdiff scripts ever run on Monad tested only the interpreter. The compiled path is evidenced only by transcriptions (cycles 10 to 13) and by mined replays, and the mined replays have no instance of the FullMath 512-bit branch, the SqrtPriceMath overflow fallback, clear, transferFrom or swaps ending on an initialized tick (theme-mined-branches). Whether the 24,009 byte runtime is compiled at all is still open after L-648, L-672 and L-676.

MegaETH: the mined-branch replay compares the sequencer's logs and storage with a revm re-execution for 1,566 transactions. That is the only check of the closed sequencer executor. L-626 (stateless validator) was again not run, for the fourth cycle running, and the same producer-only branch list as on Monad has no mined instance. high-throughput read only mega-evm v1.7.4 changelogs and file equality. The toolchain question (rust-lang issue 155241) has no answer.

HyperEVM got no network unit in cycle 13. Its closed validator is covered only by 2,762 mined replays, and 104 of the 324 multi-step swaps in theme-swap-residuals needed a tick spacing found by search, not read from an Initialize log. hl-node's revm and ruint versions (L-618) are still unknown.

Proof programs were tested on rebuilds, not on the artifacts that settle. Kona's handlers were run as a rustc 1.97 rebuild, and the prestate scan follows only straight-line code (theme-proof-builds-2 verifier). Base's SP1 range program was run as an RV64IM rebuild, not as the published ELF under Succinct's toolchain. For Celo and X Layer the release behind the range vkeys is unidentified.
